In a recent video Congressman Jim Himes in a very animated way presented his version of misleading facts attacking President Trump
Thanks for reading The Goldstein Substack! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..2dY1l1Sv71AgF2qxPfqfZG5aDxjzYfX74VglSAlbWRY?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214236306)
His speech was nothing more than false information with the intention to mislead the listener to accepting his statements as true. This propaganda is the standard operating procedure of dictatorships but has no place in our democracy.
**Tariffs**
His first attack is on tariffs against our largest trading partner, which he does not identify. It happens to be Mexico.
Goods that are covered by USMCA, which comprise 85% of the goods enter the US tax free. Non-compliant autos and other goods pay 25%. However, if a non-compliant auto contains US made parts the value of those parts is deducted from the cost used to calculate the duty. This tends to reduce the tariff with US component autos to about 15%. Vehicles by foreign manufacturers with no US components are taxed at 25%. Steel and aluminum are taxed at a higher rate.
On the other side Mexico also imposes duties.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e3ce042e-845d-4b37-a194-05406f5154e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This far from the tragic disaster presented by Jim Himes. It also results in more US jobs for auto workers by encouraging US manufacturing.
**Tax Cuts**
Himes also ranted about the effect of tax cuts on the US deficit of what he describes as $2 trillion and its effect on the bond market. This number is being spread over 10 years so only a small amount of this gets funded each year. Considering that we have $40 trillion in debt this is a very small number. What is completely negated are the benefits of no tax on tips and overtime. That money is recycled into the economy creating jobs and taxpayers.
Himes also neglects to mention Biden's Inflation Reduction Act, better known as the Inflation Creation Act. Huge amounts of money were wasted on reckless government spending. Biden a Democrat gets a Himes Pass for his mistakes.
**Immigration**
Himes in his elitist rant talks about how Trumps policies are hurting our society because there are no illegals to work in, nursing homes, restaurants and construction.
Nursing homes have skilled nurses and nursing assistants, physical therapists and physicians to take care of the medical needs of the patients. According to Himes, I guess the people that serve the food, clean the floors and toilets, wash the sheets and all of the other menial tasks must be illegals. Apparently in his elitist view is that no US citizen would do any of these menial jobs.
I have personally treated hotel workers, as patients, in NYC. They are all citizens or legal residents. They are unionized with good salaries and benefits. Every Marine carries their record. Not on a wall. In how they carry themselves for the rest of their life.

Mine says Sergeant. It says K-9 handler. It says I stood post so someone else could sleep. I didn't earn it to win an argument. I
earned it at twenty-one, working dogs on flight lines, because that was the job.

Stolen valor is serious. You do not throw that at a Marine unless you have every fact. Stephen Skoly did not have them. He
attacked anyway.

I am a United States Marine. I am the only veteran in this Republican primary. Skoly never served. One week before September 9 —
after early voting had already started — he went after my military record with a partial file and treated it like the whole story.
That is not due diligence. That is a smear.

I enlisted. I served as a military policeman and a military working-dog handler. My job was finding explosives. I was
meritoriously promoted to sergeant. I served with FAST Company, the Fleet Anti-terrorism Security Team. They issued me a letter
thanking me for the work.

How dare he tell Republican voters to doubt that service without the complete record. How dare a man who never wore the uniform
put a Marine in the stolen-valor bucket to save a sinking campaign.

He did not spend the closing weeks of this race on energy prices. Not on housing. Not on the roads we rank dead last in. He spent
it digging through a Marine's file looking for dirt.

When you attack a veteran's honorable service for political gain, you do not just disrespect one man. You disrespect every veteran
who earned the right to have that service treated with respect.

Dr. Skoly gave his word he would not run this kind of campaign. He gave it publicly. Then he broke it.

Rhode Island has more than enough politicians who say one thing and do another. We do not need one more.

If this is his judgment under pressure, what other poor judgment should we expect from him in Congress?

I'm not asking you to vote against anyone. I'm asking you to vote for a Rhode Island that stops finishing last — and for a
candidate who will not trash a veteran to get there.

We recently launched a volunteer action you can do right from your couch →
#
Hi there,
Are you constantly glued to your phone? Do you have 10+ hours of weekly screentime? We’re not going to shame you for it—we’re actually embracing it!
**Swing Left recently launched a volunteer action called social banking, and you can do it right from your couch.**
A social bank works a lot like a traditional phone bank. Volunteers gather virtually at the same time, but instead of making phone calls, we spend an hour engaging with pro-democracy content.
In 2026, control of Congress and state governments will come down to key competitive races across the country. But reaching voters today means breaking through in the places where they are already spending most of their time: Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, and Twitter.
Every like, comment, share, and full video view feeds the algorithm, pushing these posts onto the For You Pages and Instagram and Facebook Reels of everyday voters who aren't already following political accounts. When a large group of us does this together, the effect multiplies, cutting through the online noise and giving our message a huge boost.
So far, volunteers are rating this experience at an average of 93% positive, noting that the tool is easy to use, effective, and a good use of their Thursday nights.
**[We’re hosting Social Banks every Thursday at 7 pm ET, and we’d love it if you could join us!](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2248?utm_source=em20260904-2679&t=1&akid=2679%2E1562180%2Ep1vecb)**
No special experience, massive following, or technical skills are required; all you need is your phone!
**[RSVP](https://act.swingleft.org/go/2248?utm_source=em20260904-2679&t=2&akid=2679%2E1562180%2Ep1vecb)**
Thank you,
The Swing Left Team

**Since 2017, Swing Left has channeled the energy of grassroots volunteers and donors to elect Democrats, up and down the ballot, focusing on the most competitive races that can swing the national balance of power.** Right now, Swing Left is investing in grassroots organizing in key swing districts and initiatives across the country to flip the House and win the Senate and critical states in 2026. name: Mark Ronchetti
subject: Mark’s New Winter Forecast Is In 🌨️
body:
Super El Niño Is Here — But There’s a Catch | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/p6XSfVwnoC6?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| | | | | |
Mark’s New Winter Forecast Is In 🌨️New Mexico desperately needs moisture — and if you’ve seen the Rio Grande lately, you know just how serious the situation is.
So we finally gave Mark the floor (for nearly 20 minutes 😳) to answer the question so many of you have been sending us:What is REALLY happening with El Niño — and what does it mean for New Mexico this winter?
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/hO_cJ4S3_Fd?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |

🌨️ SUPER EL NIÑO IS HERE — BUT THERE’S A CATCHThe good news: The equatorial Pacific is warming dramatically and El Niño conditions are already in place. That normally favors the kind of southern storm track New Mexico desperately needs.
Mark’s early prediction?
👉 Northern New Mexico snowpack around 110% of average.After two brutal La Niña winters, that could feel VERY wet. But there’s one thing keeping him from predicting a blockbuster winter.
Ocean temperatures off the West Coast are considerably cooler than they were during the massive 1997–98 El Niño. That colder pattern — called the Pacific Decadal Oscillation — could interfere with some of the effects we normally expect from a strong El Niño.
So Mark brought back an old favorite from his KRQE days: The Bust Potential.His number right now: 35%. That means he sees roughly a 65% chance that this El Niño delivers a pretty good winter for New Mexico.
And if you're wondering whether to book the ski trip? Mark says YES.Taos. Red River. Angel Fire. Ski Santa Fe. Telluride. Wolf Creek.He especially likes the potential for the earlier part of the season.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/8U2IJoqdtKu?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🚨 65% OF NEW MEXICANS SAY NOThe data-center fight in New Mexico isn't going away. A new Albuquerque Journal poll found:
• 65% oppose large-scale data center development
• Only 20% support it
• A majority of Republicans, Democrats AND independents oppose new data centers
Those numbers are extraordinary. But we think there’s a much bigger conversation New Mexico needs to have. People have legitimate concerns about electricity rates and water — especially when we're literally walking through a dry Rio Grande. Those questions MUST be answered.
But Mark argues that simply saying “no data centers” isn't a realistic answer either. Artificial intelligence is quickly becoming a major global economic and national-security competition, and China would be more than happy to watch America decide not to build the infrastructure necessary to compete.
So where’s the balance?Data centers need to prove — with actual numbers, not talking points — that they won't raise electricity costs for New Mexico families or threaten our limited water resources. Until they do, this opposition isn't going anywhere.
🗳️ THE POLLING IS ROUGH — BUT THERE'S A CATCHWe also dig into the latest New Mexico statewide polling. Right now, several Republican candidates have significant ground to make up.
Ben Ray Luján leads Republican Larry Marker by 15 points in the U.S. Senate race, while Democrats also hold leads in several other statewide contests. We explain why money, name recognition and independent voters matter so much in these races — and why saying “polls don't matter” isn't particularly helpful.
Polls are snapshots.
The question is what campaigns DO with the information. And nationally, there's another fascinating possibility developing. If the polls are underestimating Republicans by just 2–4 points — something we've seen happen before — the Senate map looks VERY different. Michigan could flip. Texas, Iowa, Ohio and Maine could stay Republican.
And suddenly you could be looking at a 53–47 Republican Senate.
Spoiler alert: Mark isn't quite ready to guarantee it.Krysty is feeling considerably more optimistic. 😂
🏛️ FINALLY, SOMETHING AMERICA AGREES ONRepublicans and Democrats have found common ground!Unfortunately, it's this: 89% of Americans now believe corruption in the federal government is widespread.Democrats: 91%Republicans: 83%Independents: 90%
But the really fascinating part is how those numbers have changed depending on who's occupying the White House.
We break down what the numbers reveal — and why government accountability shouldn't depend on which political party happens to be in charge.
---
| [STREAM NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/uAQLh7Jp3xT?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |

🚙 AND THEN THERE'S THE $208,000 RANGE ROVER...Yes.$208,000!For an electric Range Rover. Krysty loves how they look.Mark loves reminding her how often Range Rover owners allegedly end up visiting the mechanic.This conversation goes exactly where you'd expect. 😂

I’ve been telling you for months: **we don’t panic. We prepare.** I get it. This is a big, scary attack on our election system. But as an election official in Colorado, I'm telling my county: **voters should plan to vote like they normally do.** This on-again-off-again situationship we're currently in with this USPS rule is exhausting. But as of today, it's currently blocked. That's right, we're under a new nationwide block, and**today****, the block was extended through November,** but of course the administration plans to keep appealing, right up to the Supreme Court. **This rule is reckless.** It’s unconstitutional. And fundamentally changing how an election works weeks before voting begins is an objectively terrible idea. A whistleblower inside USPS even called their work in progress to implement this rule a “shit show.” But here’s the thing about being responsible for elections: **being outraged isn’t a contingency plan.** So, I’ve been working with election officials to prepare for every possible outcome. **Your county clerk is hard at work preparing for this election.** Keep your voting plans. We’ll keep doing our jobs. That’s what competent government looks like. We use the courts to fight unlawful federal interference. **We build contingency plans for outcomes we hope never happen.** And we don’t manufacture panic or ask voters to carry the anxiety of every twist and turn in the litigation. **This fight isn’t over.** Neither is Trump's time in office. **Tales from the Trail:**
This past Wednesday was Women’s Equality Day, marking the 106th anniversary of the 19th amendment to the U.S. Constitution. Kristina started the day by holding a [press conference](https://us.list-manage.com/Dlw9n2o8S7U?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) with community leaders and women in healthcare circles outside of Mike Turner’s office. Kristina called out Mike Turner silence on against fellow Ohio representative Max Miller alleged abuse, Turner’s 64 votes against healthcare including defunding women’s healthcare facilities, and much more.

The remainder of the week was filled with incredible opportunities to meet with the community and engage with voters about the issues that are on their mind.
On Wednesday night, Team Knickerbocker held a town hall in Bellbrook at the Bellbrook Brewing Company. We would like to extend our gratitude to the owner, Julie, and their wonderful team for letting us use the space.

On Thursday, the [Black Women’s Health Imperative](https://us.list-manage.com/jG1FT8qi33y?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d) \- Dayton Chapter held a candidates’ forum where Kristina answered questions and discussed priorities for improving our community. **Mike Turner was absent, as always.** We would like to extend a huge thank you to Ms. Jacqueline and the Black Women’s Health Imperative Dayton team for their dedicated work pursuing initiatives aimed at improving health outcomes for black women and girls across the Miami Valley and state of Ohio.
****
On Friday, Kristina attended the NAACP State Convention President’s Reception where the Dayton chapter recognized the distinguished career of NAACP Ohio State Conference President Tom Roberts. President Roberts highlighted that the mission of the**biggest, baddest, boldest civil rights advocacy group** , the NAACP, will continue. Thank you, President Roberts, for your dedication and advocacy to the NAACP and for your legendary career serving the people in the great state of Ohio.
To his credit, Mike Turner showed up just long enough to present a flag to President Roberts, take a picture, and slip out the side exit -we call him- the Flash!
To kick off our Saturday and weekend, Team Knickerbocker held a canvass launch in Middletown! Thank you to all of the volunteers who helped us knock doors and get out our message that **anti-corruption, reducing the cost-of-living, and lowering healthcare** **cost** are the pillars of this campaign.

Later in the day we attended the annual Montgomery County Democrat Party Picnic where we rallied the crowd for the busy 2-months ahead. We concluded the day at a joint Labor-NAACP dinner where the guest of honor was AFL-CIO Ohio President Tim Burga. He highlighted the continued storied relationship between the labor and civil rights movement in our country. Kristina is honored to be endorsed by Ohio’s AFL-CIO so that our labor workers finally have a friend representing them in Congress.

On Sunday we went to Springfield, Ohio to attend a rally for the Haitian Immigrant population that has been subjected to the cruelty of this administration following an end to their temporary protection status. Since attending the rally, we learned more about how brutal these tactics are. After being shackled with an ankle monitor, Pierre Damas Bel died by apparent suicide on Tuesday morning. Pierre was a bright person and this nation failed him and his community. This team will continue to fight for the principles of our nation’s founding, equality and justice for all. We will not let this kind of treatment of communities, escaping war or persecution elsewhere, continue in America. [Read Kristina’s full statement here.](https://us.list-manage.com/fBsZ9XdpXST?e=36314ef925&c2id=95485440be040823d6a7108ee922ec5d)
While we work to elect new leadership in Washington, we must continue to pressure the current administration and the Senate to pass the extension of TPS. Further, Congress must pass the Haitian Refugee Immigration Fairness Act, which offers a very reasonable legal pathway to citizenship for members of this community.
We have a busy two months ahead and Team Knickerbocker is working hard to bring hope and change to the Miami Valley that it desperately needs! Save the date for events below and get involved - we need you and want you to join Team Knickerbocker!

The Supreme Court's far-right majority just ruled against us as part of the **biggest change to campaign finance law since** _**Citizens United**_**.**
**This afternoon, they decided that from this day forward, not only are there virtually ZERO limits on how much dark money national political parties can funnel to their candidates, groups like the RNC can even get a discount on advertising.**
Here's what that means: Nothing - truly, _nothing_ - is stopping the Republican Party from investing as much as they want to try to defeat Roy in North Carolina and buy this seat for our opponent in this race, who also happens to be the former chairman of the RNC.
If we lose in North Carolina, Democrats will lose our chance at taking back the Senate. The stakes couldn't be higher, so we've set a $250,000 rapid response goal for midnight tonight. [Will you chip in what you can to help us fight back against the GOP and flip this seat blue?](https://substack.com/redirect/987841a0-2a88-4e81-a64a-c41ab34611d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/987841a0-2a88-4e81-a64a-c41ab34611d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Supreme Court has just ignored the clear language of the law and given a massive TV ad discount to billionaires and other big money donors, further eroding the power of everyday people.
Former RNC Chair Michael Whatley will be first in line to benefit from the RNC's $130 million war chest to bail out his flailing campaign.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/987841a0-2a88-4e81-a64a-c41ab34611d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
With GOP super PACs already spending nearly $100 million so far on attack ads to amplify lies about Roy from Donald Trump and Stephen Miller statewide, experts were predicting this would be the first billion-dollar Senate race in history. Today, the Supreme Court basically guaranteed it.
It's clear that no amount is too high for Republicans if it protects their power and shields this lawless Administration from accountability. They're trying to silence your voice and crush our grassroots movement - and we can't let them succeed.
**We need an immediate groundswell of grassroots support to help us fight back. Otherwise, we will be drowned out by a flood of dark money in the final weeks of this race.**
[ Will you rush $5 right now, or anything you can toward our rapid-response goal to ensure we have the funds to compete with the GOP's dark money, flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate for Democrats?](https://substack.com/redirect/987841a0-2a88-4e81-a64a-c41ab34611d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/987841a0-2a88-4e81-a64a-c41ab34611d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you so much.
Jeff, Campaign Manager for Cooper for North Carolina

My message to Trump: Hands off our ballots | | | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138603890/644614595/-995582223?refcode=260904-vbm-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZmMzZmQ4ZC1jZGE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DYCvKqalzUJOz_gszqAG5iecCx-aFNvs2RNN7uN_mME=)

| | | Washington votes by mail. **_98.5% of us._** The second-highest rate in America.
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/138603891/644614596/-995582223?refcode=260904-vbm-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTkyOCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZmMzZmQ4ZC1jZGE4LWYxMTEtOWIzMy0wMDIyNDgyYTkzM2IiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=DYCvKqalzUJOz_gszqAG5iecCx-aFNvs2RNN7uN_mME=)
---
So when the Supreme Court greenlit Trump's executive order restricting mail ballots this week, that wasn't some D.C. legal story for us. That was the federal government reaching for the way an ENTIRE STATE votes. **Let me be blunt about what this order does:** it puts DC bureaucrats in charge of deciding whose ballots the Postal Service delivers. Unelected officials, 3,000 miles away, inserting themselves between you and your ballot box. I represent loggers, mechanics, farmers, and nurses — people who may not agree with each other on everything. **_But nobody in this district_****, right or left, wants the federal government touching their ballot. That's not a partisan feeling out here. That's a line.** And here's the thing about this district: we're the toss-up everyone says decides the House. They know it. That's exactly why making voting harder helps them — and exactly why I won't let it. [**Our answer isn't to panic. name: Hull for New Mexico
subject: They want to shut down New Mexico's energy jobs. I won't let them.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by [Hull for New Mexico](https://us
body:
Washington and Santa Fe keep picking winners and losers. I don't.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/9no_yLJBFgQ?e=530e36cac1&c2id=62f28c177cd28b25da81790396be4810)
| |
# All-In on New Mexico Energy
---
| | | | | | Friend,
New Mexico is one of the top energy-producing states in the entire country. Our oil and gas industry funds our schools, pays for our roads, and puts a paycheck in the hands of tens of thousands of New Mexico families.
And in Washington and in Santa Fe, there are politicians like my opponent who want to regulate it out of existence.
They'll tell you it's about the environment. It's really about control, mandates written by people who have never set foot on a rig or a solar field in New Mexico, and who don't have to answer for the jobs lost when their policies land.
I believe in an all-in energy strategy for New Mexico: oil and gas that built this state and still funds it, and solar and battery storage that prove we can lead on the next generation of energy too. Not one instead of the other. Both, because both put New Mexicans to work.
I'm not new to this fight. As Mayor of Rio Rancho, I cut the red tape that was strangling energy and business investment in our city, and I championed the Atrisco Solar Project, a $1 Billion investment that is now New Mexico's largest solar farm with battery storage. It powers more than 110,000 homes and sends tax revenue straight into Rio Rancho's public schools. I didn't just talk about energy jobs. I built them.
That's the difference between me and the politicians trying to shut this industry down piece by piece: I have actually delivered energy growth, not just a press release about it.
New Mexico's energy workers don't need Washington or Santa Fe deciding which of their jobs are allowed to exist. They need a governor who will fight for all of them.
I need your help to take this fight statewide before the people who want to shut down New Mexico energy get another term to do it. Can you chip in $25, $50, or $100 right now?

Full disclosure, I'm from Napa. This pisses me off...
**I. The Empire: A Governor with a Vineyard Portfolio**
Forbes' October 2025 investigation described a business empire built in tandem with a political career. In 1995, Newsom co-founded PlumpJack Winery with oil heir and billionaire Gordon Getty -- a family friend Forbes calls a "billionaire benefactor." From that base grew the PlumpJack Group: wineries including PlumpJack Estate, CADE Estate on Howell Mountain, Odette Estate, the Oso Vineyard in Pope Valley, and the newly acquired "13th Vineyard" estate in Angwin, plus restaurants, hotels, and wine shops -- "a power player in both Napa Valley's wine industry and San Francisco's social scene," per Forbes.
Forbes combed Newsom's state financial disclosures, real estate records, and PlumpJack's websites to map the holdings. Its bottom line: the wineries alone are worth over $400 million, meaning even Newsom's minority stake could be worth tens of millions of dollars. Some pieces of the empire -- a wine retailer among them -- have shuttered, but the core vineyards have been enormously successful.
Newsom's spokesperson Nathan Click declined to comment on any holding or stake, reiterating only that the governor's assets sit in a blind trust. Forbes, writing as Newsom is rumored to be gearing up for a White House bid, notes the practical effect: management may be walled off, but the wealth -- and its appreciation -- still flows to the governor's family.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9b3d719-ddec-47bc-833a-93de639826b1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**II. The Money Trail: $2 Million a Year -- and the DOJ at the Door**
Fortune's August 1, 2026 report covered Newsom's release of more than 700 pages of tax returns covering 2022-2024, revealing that the governor and First Partner Jennifer Siebel Newsom earned between $1.7 million and $2 million per year -- income anchored, as the filings show, in investments and salaries flowing from his business past rather than his roughly $210,000 state salary. The couple paid roughly half a million dollars in taxes annually on those earnings. Notably, the returns for 2025 -- the most recent and most sensitive year -- were withheld, because the Newsoms filed an extension and will complete those filings in October.
The release came amid a Justice Department investigation. In mid-June 2026, Newsom announced that he and the First Partner are under federal scrutiny; his office published a fact sheet declaring it "sure the subpoenas are coming" and that "the governor looks forward to it." Follow-on reporting by CalMatters and KCRA indicates the probes -- reportedly originating from whistleblower tips -- focus in part on Siebel Newsom's finances and the nonprofits she leads, including Girls Club Entertainment and The Representation Project, and on "behested payments" -- corporate gifts to charities made at a politician's behest -- long flagged as California's corruption vector. Newsom's office calls the investigation politically motivated retaliation by Trump's DOJ and has demanded records of it; prominent Washington defense attorney Abbe Lowell has been retained. No charges have been filed.
KCRA's tax experts added a cautionary note: the returns don't show the full picture of the Newsoms' wealth -- trusts holding more than $1 million in assets, and a wine business Forbes valued at $400 million, sit largely outside what a joint federal return reveals.
**III. First in Line at the Fire Payout**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0e8a0529-347f-4c8d-a912-fb7eb56db665?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A Free Republic item -- Greenfield's Frontpage piece built on San Francisco Chronicle and Daily Mail reporting -- records the moment Napa growers' patience broke. The Pickett Fire ignited near Calistoga in August 2025 on land associated with Hundred Acre Winery and burned roughly 6,800 acres over 17 days, destroying grape crops across the valley. The Chronicle tallied about $56 million in wine-grape losses; more than 30 small wineries and vineyard owners are seeking up to $90 million from Hundred Acre and its owner, Jayson Woodbridge, with civil suits now filed and a winery gardener charged with igniting the blaze.
Of all those claimants, exactly one has been paid: the PlumpJack Group, co-founded by Newsom. PlumpJack lost 60 of the 129 acres of vines at its Oso Vineyard in remote Pope Valley -- a real and substantial burn -- while most other claimants suffered smoke damage to their grapes and one other winery lost a single acre. The size of PlumpJack's settlement from Hundred Acre is undisclosed. The company said it was "grateful to put this matter behind us," and denied "any speculation that Newsom was involved in the settlement process."
Growers still waiting are furious. Local radio headlined it bluntly: "Vineyard Owners Outraged Only Newsom Wines Gets Settlement." As Wine-Searcher's summary of the same story noted, the blind trust doesn't change the outcome for Newsom personally: it means he "doesn't do day-to-day management; he still gets his share of the payout."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/77339d52-a9ac-48fc-bca8-a3048352ed08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**IV. The Pattern Critics See -- and What the Governor's Side Says**
Read together, the three reports describe a governor whose personal fortune is entangled with the industry he regulates, whose most recent tax year remains sealed until after a presidential campaign heats up, and whose winery jumped the compensation line in a disaster that crushed dozens of his neighbors. To critics -- Napa growers, the Free Republic poster sphere, and the DOJ itself -- the word for that is greed: rules for thee, profits for me.
The governor's side disputes every part of that framing: PlumpJack insists the settlement was handled without him; the blind trust was established when he took office precisely to prevent day-to-day involvement; his released returns show compliance and half-million-dollar annual tax payments; and the DOJ probe, his office argues, is a partisan weapon that has so far produced no charges and no investigator interviews. Those defenses are not trivial, and none of the three articles documents an actual crime. Greenfield's piece, in particular, is openly opinion-driven commentary layered over Chronicle reporting -- its characterizations are contested.
But the questions the reporting raises are fair ones only transparency can answer: Why is the 2025 return -- the year of the fire settlement -- due only in October? Why is the only settled wildfire claim in Napa the one with a governor's name attached? And can a blind trust blind anything when the asset at its center bears the owner's brand?
And while we're in Napa -- here's a detail that puts the whole valley in a different light. The Pelosis. Aunt Nancy and Uncle Paul. Yes, that Pelosi. Paul Pelosi -- the same Paul Pelosi whose stock trades have made him a legend on Wall Street -- has held a stake for decades in a five-star hillside resort overlooking the vineyards of Rutherford. You've heard of it: the Auberge du Soleil. Rooms there run up to two thousand dollars a night. It's the crown jewel of Napa luxury -- Michelin-starred restaurant, Provence-style cottages, the works. The Pelosi family's other Napa holdings -- a vineyard, the resort -- made Nancy Pelosi up to a million dollars a year. The vineyards of Napa aren't just wine country, folks. They're where the political class goes to park its money.
And how did that resort spend the pandemic? In 2021, the Auberge du Soleil -- a luxury hotel charging a grand a night -- took in millions in COVID-19 bailout money. Paul Pelosi had held that investment for decades, and for most of those years it barely turned a profit. Then came the pandemic -- the pandemic year, when small businesses across America were dying -- and suddenly the Pelosis' income from the resort surged to between one and five million dollars, more than they'd made on it in years. RealClearInvestigations tallied it up: an unreported twenty-eight million dollars in pandemic grants funneled to that luxury hotel. A resort with rooms that cost more per night than many Americans make in a week -- rescued with taxpayer money by the same woman who ran the House when the bailout bill was written. And Gavin Newsom's Napa, remember, is the same Napa where the Pelosis vacation. These are not strangers. This is one club, and we're not in it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/81dce030-1639-430a-b88e-24d3f93a360e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**V. The Crush**
The Forbes portrait establishes scale: a nine-figure wine fortune assembled alongside two decades in public office. The Fortune report establishes money in motion: up to $2 million a year in disclosed income, a sealed 2025 filing, and a federal investigation circling the family's finances. The Frontpage/Free Republic item establishes the flashpoint: a valley full of unpaid, smoke-damaged growers -- and one winery, the governor's, already paid. One money losing resort, the uncle's, procured. Whatever the final verdict of investigators or voters, the pattern now under scrutiny in Napa's vineyards is, at minimum, a serious optics problem for a likely 2028 presidential candidate -- and, in critics' telling, a case study in a politician treating public office and private gain as the same vineyard row.

## Judge Declares Mistrial in Clancy Case
A judge [declared a mistrial](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkMGOrCAQRb9GdxhEBV2weBt3_bazNCWUNp0SDNCa_vuJzvzB7E5SlZt77tdjeoAj59f_sKHOS5g8nokwZ4yTIfDms7mUowMygQhXXELIk-BCMj4w3k1gsjtwaqG0ekEU2JSoa9X3kgslVfnUEuq5aWpQ3WxNJ_k8dGLpwQwolLFSlE5feXzgXc255G0Fom172y04SG77HouWo3U5xOoVnM9PXOgTDoyVCVtJ-pnznormXyHGQozneVZ-NpfHdS_EeGEhxndiv0TuQDZTWG_2NsGH_ciyW5XdD-_dQsbELC7oEzLYdwRK7PW2KzIDnlk0BBHZ5lg0HrqhVUqUUdv9dEQuSVW0fN3A0d00_3HgQ4vvAAAA__9lppLz) Friday in the sensational Lindsay Clancy murder trial after jurors remained deadlocked through 36 hours of deliberations. Clancy is accused of strangling her three children in their Duxbury, Massachusetts home in 2023. Clancy's attorney argued that a lone holdout juror [refused to follow the law](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2OpDAMwPGngS7I5IOPIsU1dHPtlSgkBjIKZJQYEG9_mllts-2WlqW__PO_x_gwPvh9-Ws21DTHcccrByTCNNpgdntvPlPyJtgYAi44x0gjB94w6Bmo0VjyJ47SlE7PiBxFibpuu64B3jZtuequkbUSQvVKQi-MmqGdajEJYTszqdmVXr970IOqARqQleFSdk7N2Dfgug4LCeg8xVQ9o99pxTnc8cRU2biVQa9Er1yIPwUfCj5c11XZKb8d733BhylminvBh-BPZMfLGcL8GXeXzc2-nGw7ksPEPli2HvvCnke62befnZict8QuQ3ZlP1pl0u51-RB8btpCwrIZHz730S_femr-PwAA__-oMZBR) on reasonable doubt and appealed immediately to Massachusetts' highest court, seeking an order to investigate and potentially remove him from the panel. The appeal was denied. Clancy's defense conceded she killed the children but argued postpartum psychosis left her not criminally responsible. She [remains held without bail](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u7CAQRp8Gd1gsxn8FxV5duduUSWnNwmBPhMECstbm6SMnyhOkmuJIo--ct9t8A_IUlhfYUBcX54BH9lgKptl4COa5US6JwJvoPS7oYiyzFLLjYuSincEUeuCsoLLaIUpsKtSXfhg6Ifuur1bt-sbBcIfGwiAVwugQGtsKdBclxhYq0uc_MYr2IkQnVA1SqcG2DsdO2GFApgRaKjHV75FCWdH5Z3xgqk3cKq_XUvbMmiuTE5PTcRz1lsPJmJww8I_M5HRqnTAmb8-7QuEr7DuGzMlx4L-anDK3aDwktJwC9xRshif_icENZGRygsSvV3n_9EtmzRQNWdb8_3d2xCO_YtqrpO1-kPeUu54psWxA_ntv-WPmh5ZfAQAA___7bJTl) at a state psychiatric facility while prosecutors decide whether to retry the case.
## Jobs Reports Blows Past Forecasts
The U.S. economy [added 162,000 jobs](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQxvGnsTusAduAC4o07i5tSouDsT0nDCuY3YvfPtrkEdL_9OnT_9fH9uEpUT5--gsd72XL-N0SMmPdQvI53Bc1ruRTKCnhgXspvClQWsAiYN58YHrhNvk-uh1R4dijk8ZaDcpo059ujAhWgjIWPuWopTFWjvOuzGKlgWXuyb33YIFZAmiYBq-mycZ5x0VDtBa7CTASlzp8Fcp84p7u8sI6hHL1yZ3Mj9aNPzq1dmrdKfsccLj9WcpbdGrFUHK57k6tvjKFhJ1an034GDEKqRUAiK_y2QRl4Z_Hs7Fol28n5UPg7wcG9kwlt3-o4qNUFtLMWk5K6uHkK_XVxcc3pURNm26C4_KU_h7k_-z6cupPAAAA__-I84zF) in August, more than doubling economists' forecasts and delivering the strongest month of hiring since March. The unemployment rate held steady at 4.1%. Food services led the gains with 59,000 new positions, followed by public education at 42,000. The Labor Department [also revised](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdEbLYgwULv6GLn97JTJmTZwzOLI3QXn7E_cK14000oy-7-s232yI4dj-250M-zQfdJZIzJRnF-3hPnsonIONLsVIG_mUeEZALWGU0M3WcXjTrGy1Gk-E1FZkmn4YNGCv--pukHTnm67t3KDRKoC2d2gXR9o37bhSFcy1ByN0DYAGVVtUalg7T6OGdRhIKKA1cMr1I4WD7-TjJ70p1y7tVTR35mcR7T-Bk8DpPM_aLeXiuHqB0xUFTva1vQrLR1qKzPRMmeWryGiXlOVu8zexwKnKZn2eIcZQdC8UbLsN8feH_6jnbfAnAAD__2c2e2o) July's initially negative figures into positive territory. The stronger-than-expected report complicates [the Federal Reserve's decision](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpCAUhZ8GOw0yIFJQbGM3225pEC_OnSAYuI6Zt9_4v8Jfn5Nz8n3_nvPTYcS0_XU7WAp5TnDVCERQZh9d8t8dKxV00ecYYYOQM82Ci6HlpuVqdp7wA7N0zWoDgIBHA7bX4zhwoQfdvOzSD6sCH4RTykivnV9Gcxe0EaJ_6AbtvccNVz3nA5edE1KOqwpgBr6OIzDJYUXKpXtnTPSCEL_5A6XzeW-ifREdlT3-MDExMV3X1aXF3xx3zsS0nBUT1MrEBD6nvH-ZmNy5nZXad15qW-DIhVoq5360mEJ0hDm1xSenjDJaNsWux4UxYh00k3zbHcafd_qltI8V_wMAAP__RyeDNg) ahead of its Sept. 15-16 meeting, where officials are weighing whether to raise rates to combat persistent inflation.
## College Football Set for Kickoff
College football’s first full [Saturday slate](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFuhDAMgOGnCduhYDgIQ4Yu2a5rx8gE50hrCCLpId6-StU36Ozf1id_POwDA4ft-Y4r6eyj3ehMTDnTYR3j5q41pHwEZBeZ6Uk-xmxBQn-T403eLbocXmQ7rGbtiYDainQzKNVLGPqhWjSi8oTtqKhtJ0Wja71qceoah-CnqamCLvfkKO-NlL3saoSuU_Pd09jLWSkSnaQ55HjUnzFseSHPV3zRUbu4VqyXnPck2jcBRoA5z7OmtG9lKMD8sW_FPSGzAJPcQvM3kwBjywLRlwDTCDAX4SHAFE7pCFPc8rWXEqpDz_sZmEPqB9HJ54qBfwX5n497afgJAAD__wavgqs) has arrived, with No. 2 Oregon hosting Boise State this afternoon before Clemson and No. 11 LSU take center stage tonight in Baton Rouge.

ESPN’s [_College GameDay_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGurCAQBuCnwQ4zjIhYUNyGbm97S8PKqNxFMciu8e1PdnPOE5x6Mn--__93G24uxLDNf91Kpkxp2Og8IpVCeRij28ZrDUfJwcUxxUgzTSmVAQEVh55DO7ixhBcN0lXeTERITUVGdForwE511WIaBd3kAbTo765F6pxXU69BiuYuGuGqYN550EMrABTI2qGU2rcT9Qq81sQkkA8l5fp_CltZaIpXelGux7RW0Syl7Adr_jC0DO15njUd-_Y-MrTfbP52312MDO1RUr4Y2oGhDZ6hlb0WqkNkaD_Nfn5mt5J3Fz-JHlzw1ZVxee58ftJR-B7GB2W-pkxVNn4_Q4zhUB2TMK8uxA-u_HLTl8GvAAAA__-WYIsb) will be live from LSU’s campus for the program’s 500th road show as Lane Kiffin prepares to make his LSU coaching debut after a tumultuous offseason.

On Thursday, the Southeastern Conference filed a federal lawsuit against LSU and Kiffin over the program’s push to roster former NFL players. Later that day, a Louisiana judge separately [granted a preliminary injunction](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdEbGgIHCRRq6lzYlmthjmKfBXuHZRfv30eYXXn2lq3POn6_tC4gp77_hRC-pbBnvyiiC1xYYcnifVOUi4FCYccdUimzWWKfNos24QRB64TZAE31CtNg36Ltpnp2xk5uaw4-xm4Jz3QxLmhx0ZgppxCXNne36JYSG_OfPLGbsjHFmaMEOwxzHhIszcZ5RDQYjSbna70JZDkz8Li-82lDOhv0h8qiq_6Xsqux633dbcv_ZlF0_OsquXJ5UCTLo72fcUUcMTBmrlqIr5CBUss4BQFcMOpVLy3EhCGbKu35gBhbCqilrZNrpLzHJWzPc9Umi7NpcPj5uYqbqJjWY_QTi_3zyw6wvb_8FAAD___3_kI0) allowing dozens of athletes, including former pros recruited by LSU, to pursue another season of eligibility.

Nationally, Ohio State [opens the season at No. 1](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1urDAQhZ_GdEZmMH-Fi9vQ7W1TogGPWSeDjWxr0b59RJQ3SH2kc77zfTyWB3r2Yf-PB5ni4hLoykylUFo2xrC9D59L8shbZKadXIxlAQW9VJNU3YJb8S9aNFbWOCKgtiLTDOPYKxj6oXoamKBz29rYdtUwtN3o9EagBqdt07qVKm_uPjWprlGqV7pG0Hq0naOpV3YcSWhF1peY6s_oQ3mS43d8Uaq3eFRsnqWcWbT_BMwC5uu66hjaOxMw33cEzL_w8qZfkVkmDF8-7FmeiTJhjkHiKc_ILEs8JXQyERNmsgLmKhl7Xp7Z534QWu0Hev4ZL3909jLwHQAA___YpILD), with Oregon, Georgia, Notre Dame, and Texas rounding out the top five. ## Trump Approves Texas Flood Disaster Aid
President Trump approved a [major disaster declaration](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSozAQRL8GMlGSDAgFCi4h86UXUmM0YPmERGlmwfv3W3b5Dzbu6u5X7991ukKIIa1_YUPHzyVPCU-KyIxlKpD-o2eEjW64hkQIlBNxmbTUvZBWyG6CmcOBUwu1dzfprarRKTMMveyV1fXdKbuAlXrwuAzKdnpQ0hujAU0Lpp9VHdxrTlrZKSUv0ja3uVsMamte1dn0VSvRB86l4TsyPoGW-J0PLM2ctzq6O_NO1eVPpcdKj-d5Ngtu0Kz5qPS4FyQSBSMCYaXHz9flEwWPiYXPCaIXD8Hla9sF7HvJB5LY4JGL8IGAGIvwOEcowCEn8eaoi_P7GWIM1JuqlesGIb6p-Lc2D6d_AgAA__-UsYyA) Thursday for 19 Texas counties battered by July's floods. The declaration covers Hill Country counties, including Kerr, Kendall, Gillespie, and Uvalde, funding [emergency work and repairs](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkD1ywyAUhE-DOjSA_kxBkUad06bUPImHRIzAA8-SffuMfYXUO7uz3_dzna7gg4_rN-xo6OnSFPEsAYkwTxniDS0h7GXG1ceCUFIslCclVM-F5qKbYCF_4NRCZc0srJYVGjlcLr3opVbVZhqrlHKuQXGxIEXba2hQ6qGDVizDPFfevOeEFp2UohG6npfODaj0ILWDZehZK9B6SrmmDQmfUFx4pQNzvaS9CmYjuhfWfDE1MjWe51nfnhDfIVPjm4ep8VNjaoR5TkQcYkyPuGDhDi1mCBxK8YUgLshdyvz3EV684IEZ-YlAG2buQkrWx5Vb2GFFpsYqG3s_fQi-9ANrxbqDD59X9F-bh1F_AQAA__-1JI23) to public infrastructure. Texas previously had only an emergency declaration, capped at $5 million. Requests covering nine more counties, plus [individual assistance](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGSnDAQRL8GMlGSWNAqUOBks3PqkBrQiFVZaKjRHHv-e9etP8Fxd3X1e78-lg_IJdf9JxwY5CvRUvHVCoogLwz1N0ZBONqKe64NoVFtwovVdlbaKz0tsEm-cLlBH8Oqozc9BuPu91nPxtv-Ge7eOevHMd2Ni1uENOEYx9ElPeFk0q3P4XtOez0Zo0fth3WbkkPrnfEJNjd3N40xC_EgTxT8gpbKH7qQh42OvoSnyNm68UdnH5197HQN79Kw09XZxzdQZx8nNfmXIldiBetKIgpqpc-6YVMJIzIUFXODJsgq4laAQTJVBefJdEFRiVi1z-NAVg0vZFQvBHkiK6hRpUIUc917DvF85VJym1130_sBubzfyv9avoL9GwAA__8SY5fS) for temporary housing and repairs in 30 counties, remain pending. In Kerr County, where the Guadalupe River flooded for a second straight year, more than 800 homes were damaged.
## Abbott Presses Feds over $10B Medicaid
Gov. Greg Abbott is pressing the Trump administration to [release nearly $10 billion](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUDuSnDAQPY3INCV6AI0CAidk69QhpU8DXSskSmqG9e1dzBWcvOj9_3zNX5YipfW33XHknyXPCa8akRnLXGz6xsBo9-pwpVTR1pwqlxkUDFIZqfrZeqY3zp1twuhUMG2DY6tfr0ENrYFmG8GobmjDC3SAodW9WoLun53rtHev3mFD422njOrbVj2VeTjfLxrB6NYs1utBdAoDcS4P3pDxx9Yl_s1vLA-f9yaOG_NRxfOXgEnAdF3Xw0fy37Dls3JON0vAdA8TMH30AqY7U8CkzA0gYFrzW64FV2mdy8wy5NNFrDLkK8mNqqznceTCMidZbEF5nC6SlwutG8slF7ljIG8pyOVMgdIqYGrKGI6LYqQ6aNGpdbcUP7X5f-9-j_AvAAD__wfUlmE) in Medicaid funding withheld from Texas hospitals. Hospitals pay about $4.2 billion a year in local taxes that draw matching federal dollars. Regulators began questioning that structure last December and froze the money, which was due to start flowing on Tuesday. Hospitals expect to lose [$27 million a day](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO8yAQhZ8Gd1iAL4SC4m_c5W-3tMYwtlEwWGY2Tt5-5Uj7BNvNRd_ROefrPt4hxJCW_7Chpdecx4RniUiEx3hAeqAnhK1MuIRUEEpOhY5RCdVzYbjoRnAUnji2UHk7CW9khVbq260XvTSqWq1wavLCtFpir1GBFKrv2tlgY9D4qamCveSEEZ2UohGmnlw3a1RGSzOD0z1rBfpA-ahpRcIXlDm-8xOP2uWtinYl2gtr_jE1MDWc51m7qVw5rj9TwwdharhOvytfc9kDQSwcXzs64pR5zAW50nwLMYacOHAPbx4S39AHB8Hz-Tv5kBZeCA66BlpD4Sfig6mhOqzfz4stvWatWDYI8eOR_trt06qfAAAA__8k45IW) during the standoff. In a letter to Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., Abbott called the hold an economic "gun to the head." His office says the financing "fully complies with federal law," but has [offered to update](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLuO2zAQAL-G6mQsKUs0CxZp1F3alMKSXElE-DDIPcv390GST7h-MBjMr4_tA2OK5fiJmSy_97oVunoiZmpbw_KbAhPm7uiIpRP2Wjq3TYFaRjAjzBt6ji_a7jgE6yAYOZCV-vFYYJFGDaelaXaTAzKkPEojH3JWGjQgmjBpcEO0f3VgYJYSJjA35-ddkzJamh29XsQdKESu7cYnMb2x7-mrvqjdfM1Dsifzs4vph1CrUOt1XbcL-xnLwbXQG3Ms_1Gh1mdN0X8JtZ6EiU-PjYRa71oq0FKoFZ2rzGOgjCWM3D7zc2zUuTYaM4XoMYZx_ywhlkOodWg2PK-YUuyLFnc4Msb0r4q_e_Nl1Z8AAAD__-acjDo) the tax structure if Washington guarantees Texas won't lose funding.

This week Missouri made the news when the Missouri Supreme Court [unanimously rejected](https://substack.com/redirect/abc63538-5b1c-48b1-aa67-80a5e5d1c8fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the Republican Secretary of State's attempts to force through a new congressional map without first putting it to a vote of the people (who had requested a referendum via signature gathering). The heavily Republican-appointed court chastised him for essentially playing games with his position and ignoring the law.
The immediate practical impact of this decision is that, barring intervention by the US Supreme Court, Missouri will retain its 6-2 Republican-advantaged map rather than the 7-1 map President Trump had pushed the governor and legislature to adopt off-cycle. Retaining the old map essentially guarantees Republicans one fewer seat in Congress from Missouri and also actually leaves a competitive seat outside of St. Louis that could shift things even more.
This decision is yet another piece of evidence that Missouri is shockingly more progressive than most people realize. Don't believe me? Then read on!
Lucas's Substack is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9sdWNhc2t1bmNlLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.0Jml-nLJy-nW61K9patuasELpfQCbZhPGytpvYA7oUA?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=214217328)
The Supreme Court's decision comes directly on the heels of the people of Missouri resoundingly rejecting its governor and legislature's marquee regressive tax proposal to eliminate the state income tax [by a shockingly large margin of 83% to 17%](https://substack.com/redirect/54948ece-964a-42df-9afd-885820ac87cb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Here's where it gets interesting. The people of Missouri have been rejecting the policies of their elected representatives over and over and over again in the last decade since Republicans took control of both the Governor's office and state legislature. [Check these results out](https://substack.com/redirect/e5590aac-1c6a-4539-b890-dacb33ce758b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
1. In 2024, voters passed an initiative increasing the minimum wage to $15/hour and adjusting it annually based on the CPI, and requiring employers to provide paid sick leave to employees; 58%-42%.
2. In 2024, voters amended the constitution to make abortion before fetal viability a constitutional right; 52%-48%.
3. In 2022, voters amended the constitution to legalize recreational marijuana; 53%-47%.
4. In 2020, constitutionally expanded Medicaid; 53% to 47%.
5. In 2018, increased the minimum wage to $12/hour; 62%-38%.
6. In 2018, legalized medical marijuana 66%-34%.
7. In 2018, passed election, campaign finance, anti-corruption, and anti-lobbying reforms; 62%-38%.
8. In 2018, rejected the governor and legislature's anti-union "right to work" legislation; 33%-67%.

Every single one of these votes overcame intense lobbying, pressure, and media campaigns conducted by the governor and state legislature. And yet many of them passed by huge amounts and are more progressive than you would have found in many so-called "blue" states when they were passed, or than you would even find now.
Frustrated by their own citizens consistently overturning their policy through popular referendum, the governor and legislature actually sought to destroy Missouri's initiative petition process on the same ballot as the income tax repeal measure this August, so that they could go back to making all the decisions for us without interference. I suppose they figure they are smarter than the people of Missouri and know what's best for us regardless of what we want (quite the irony considering the anti-elite and often populist campaign slogans many of them were elected on).
[Well, they lost that effort, too, by another massive margin of 80% to 20%](https://substack.com/redirect/eb887048-8905-47a3-84e1-ff483342e002?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). In fact, neither that nor the income tax repeal measure passed _in a single one of the 114 Missouri counties or the City of St. Louis_ , and it wasn't close in any of them.
I imagine many of you, especially if you're outside of Missouri, are shocked by these consistently progressive results considering the reputation the state has and the makeup of its elected officials. Or possibly even after reading [my last post about the state of my old neighborhood in Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/a1c86060-2d57-43e5-8c47-3b9a4357bd1f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Although I'd suspect that even that grumpy old neighborhood voted for all of those people-powered reforms except the abortion one.
So what gives? Perhaps people feel like as long as they can overrule their elected officials on policy they can pick ones they are more comfortable with on culture? I'm curious what others think in the comments, from either side of the aisle. But, as I've said before, I'd caution anyone from asking the question "why do people vote against their own self interest" without thinking about it more, something I've gone deep on here in the past:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/5394f6e6-84d7-461b-8fae-0d3fec031dcf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### ["Why do people keep voting against their own self-interest?"](https://substack.com/redirect/5394f6e6-84d7-461b-8fae-0d3fec031dcf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

name: Carole King
subject: I’m focused on New Hampshire
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260905_1.h4RJ2m&refcode=em20260905-1&t=1001&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]Carole King

Hi, it’s
Carole King 🎵and I personally wrote this email.

John E. Sununu is the latest in the New Hampshire family of men named
Sununu vying for political power. John E. is running for the U.S. Senate,
and there’s a difference between vying and serving.

Chris Pappas has been serving constituents in New Hampshire’s 1st district
in the U.S. House, and now he’s running to serve every Granite Stater in
the U.S. Senate.

I know Chris personally, and he is worthy.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260905_1.h4RJ2m&refcode=em20260905-1&t=1002&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]Will you give $1, $5, or whatever you can afford right now to help
Chris earn the votes of more people in New Hampshire?

If elected, John E. would likely join other Senate Republicans in voting
for whatever the person in the White House wanted no matter how irrational
or illogical or corrupt. And if an opening occurred on the Supreme Court,
Sununu would likely confirm the president’s nominee as another justice to
take more of our rights away.

Chris Pappas will vote for whatever and whoever will lift hardworking
individuals and families out of the financial, medical, and other worries
that this president cares nothing about.

“I don’t think about Americans’ financial situation,” said the President
on May 12th. “Not even a little bit.” And on August 14th he said, “...when
you have to pay a little bit more, you’re at four dollars. It’s okay...
I’ll never apologize. I did the right thing.”

It’s more than four dollars, and it’s not okay. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260905_1.h4RJ2m&refcode=em20260905-1&t=1003&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]We need Senator
Pappas’s vote in the Senate to rein. this. president. in.

We don’t know whether Sununu would have voted for the resolution directing
the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities with Iran. But
we do know that Chris Pappas voted YES on June 3rd to bring our military
family members home.

It appears that the Sununu family has a close relationship with power and
money and maybe not as close with everyday people.

Chris Pappas IS everyday people. And that’s why he needs our help to pay
for gas to travel around the state and meet with folks across party lines
wherever they are.

Will you contribute a few dollars—or more if you can afford it—to help
Chris do more of that? If your number isn’t in a box, click OTHER and
enter your amount.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260905_1.h4RJ2m&amount=5&refcode=em20260905-1&t=1022&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]Donate $5 »

I really
appreciate you giving whatever you can afford to help Chris win by a
decisive margin on November 3rd. You may not think your donation makes a
difference, but small donations really do add up.

Whether you donate large, small, or not at all, here are two other ways
you can support Chris for free.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/695?t=1023&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]Vote.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/signup/take_action_pappas_campaign/?source=em20260905-1&t=1024&akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt ]Volunteer.

Whatever you do, don’t be discouraged. I
find it helpful to know that I’m part of a growing movement to replace
corruption and depravity with hope and humanity. I hope you take some
comfort in knowing that you, too, are part of the movement. I wish you and
your family all the best. Stay strong. We’ll get through this.

- Carole

Carole King is a singer-songwriter, author, and activist. Her
distinctions include a Grammy Lifetime Achievement Award, a Kennedy
Center Honor, and double-induction into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame.
Now Carole is using her platform to help elect candidates who are
running to lift and improve the lives of their fellow Americans. And she
really did write this email.

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=8733%2E582294%2EcVrRTt

subject: Confront the Marxist lies on the battlefield of education
body:
Is human nature fixed, or can it be changed? That question lies at the heart of some of the most consequential ideas in history.

This sponsored message from Inside Scoop Politics is on behalf of Hillsdale College
| | | [](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckc2K2zAQgJ9GvtnIkmLLBx-WOoGFZkubQ3szijS2B_SHNU77-CU0fYG9ft_wDcz8vM5Xgx7j-mECjFjK7JKbbYrLniLRBsHsf7CQRygp0iy46Go-1Pw0G0v4gFmZyo0n0epFVzC2vdYdH7TQ1Taq9m6hb_XS3q0QSi192-vFONepuzXaVDg-e3zgp1ZwqWTjOrUMAwxD36vWLAtT_MjOEDQYCzooNqWck0dCW5q0r5UfN6JcmHxj4sLEpYA9dmg29L4446EBdzBxcSkagqc_ck471bRBjR6NY_JSYA0Q6UtywOTEJW_lBxdKfD1P07fpfL4x0R0U5pKO3T5H8p5KBksY15cK4PAITE4QDPoXtCZkg2tkcvq36oVTJIjE5HR9-_Hr_Xadv_f1--1W_z9GtY8u_0bvsXQ9U3x9NhubQkWffdFjFH8DAAD__zsIoxQ)
---
| | Dear Fellow American, **Is human nature fixed, or can it be changed?** That question lies at the heart of some of the most consequential ideas in history. Karl Marx believed that if society could be upended, mankind itself could be remade. That promise inspired revolutionary movements throughout the twentieth century—with catastrophic consequences, as communist regimes claimed the lives of more than 100 million people. **Sadly, we’re seeing a resurgence of this destructive ideology right here in the United States.** But anyone who’s read Homer understands something far different. Nearly **3,000 years ago** , _The Iliad_ portrayed men and women with the same hopes, fears, loves, jealousies, ambitions, courage, and grief that we recognize today. Open its pages, and you discover something remarkable: **Human nature has not changed.** Near the end of the poem, King Priam of Troy enters the camp of Achilles, the warrior who killed his beloved son Hector. The old king kneels before his enemy and begs for his son’s body. Achilles thinks of his own aging father, and both men weep together. Every parent understands that scene. Every son can understand it. Across three millennia, Homer reminds us that what is deepest in human nature remains the same. That is why _The Iliad_ has endured as one of the foundational works of Western civilization. And it is one reason Hillsdale College created our free online course, **“The Iliad.”** The course introduces students to truths about courage, honor, sacrifice, friendship, justice, and duty—truths that every generation must rediscover if liberty is to endure. The damage is done.

While politicians can shake hands and proclaim that the war is over, the reality is the decimation of the Persian Gulf’s energy infrastructure can’t be fixed with a “deal.”

A peace treaty can’t rebuild a liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) facility that took 14 years and $50 billion to build... and all across the Middle East, energy infrastructure has been decimated.

Qatar's Ras Laffan facility handled about 100 million tonnes of LNG per year, nearly a third of the entire global supply. It has been destroyed.

The CEO of QatarEnergy, Saad al-Kaabi, said publicly that repairs will take _"three to five years."_ Three to five years. That's not a political problem. That's an engineering problem.

Saudi Aramco's Ras Tanura, the world's largest offshore oil loading terminal, was hit. Iran's own South Pars gas field, the largest natural gas field on the planet, has been struck.

Oil infrastructure across the region that took decades and hundreds of billions of dollars to construct has been laid to waste.

The International Energy Agency, the same body that has tracked every oil crisis since 1973, issued an alarming statement:

_"The war in the Middle East is creating the largest supply disruption in the history of the global oil market."_

That’s because this time it’s _physical._

Consider the embargo of 1973, that was political and could be reversed with a deal. Or the Iranian Revolution of 1979, which disrupted production but left infrastructure intact.

This time, the infrastructure is rubble.

And the devastation cannot be undone with a “deal.”

I didn’t enter this race as a career politician or corporate insider. I stepped up because working families across North Alabama—from Cullman to Walker, Blount, and beyond—deserve a representative focused on what genuinely matters at the kitchen table: protecting rural hospitals, lowering everyday costs, and ensuring honest accountability.
Our campaign doesn’t run on big corporate PAC checks. It runs on neighbors pitching in what they can.
As we head into the homestretch of this election cycle, **we have set a clear, grassroots goal to raise $5,000 by the end of September.**
Hitting this milestone allows us to:
* Fund targeted outreach across our district's communities to ensure every voter knows they have a real choice.
* Equip our volunteer teams with voter contact tools, phone-banking resources, and organizers on the ground.
* Keep our grassroots momentum strong without relying on special interests.

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

subject: Please come join us celebrating Mississippi’s success!
body:
| | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/mspolicy/thewire-12854693?e=5703353baa)
---
| |
---
| _**If you're not in front of our Saturday email, you're behind.**_
---
| Dear Friend,
Would you like to have fun celebrating Mississippi’s success?
---
| [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/dARaqpxmOOY?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3)
---
| **Come to our Gala to celebrate our state!**

For decades Mississippi was told it sat 50th out of 50. Last on every table. A punchline. Hollywood treated the state with open condescension.

Not anymore.

**Young Americans choosing college are heading to SEC states in droves** , and Mississippi’s campuses are among the winners — drawing students who want an education, not a seminar on microaggressions.

Businesses are following. Hardly a week passes without Bill Cork and the Mississippi Development Authority announcing another major investment.

**This is the Boom Belt!**
---
|
---
| [Reserve Your Tickets Here](https://us.list-manage.com/nu1mW8boapC?e=5703353baa&c2id=0d4484d08dfcd99680c1a241a59ef3e3 "Reserve Your Tickets Here")
---
| As Mississippi’s free market think tank, we exist to honor the policies and people who built this growth story. That is what our annual Gala is for — and we would be delighted if you joined us.

**Grover Norquist** of Americans for Tax Reform and **Charles C.W. Cooke** of National Review will discuss Mississippi’s rise as a leader in free-market reform and one of the standout Boom Belt states.

We are also proud to welcome **Speaker Jason White** as a keynote speaker. He has been at the center of the state’s progress, advancing a clear vision of growth, opportunity, and prosperity for every Mississippian.
