## **Hey, Angry Patriots!**
Welcome to _The Angry Files_ , the politics on my radar this week.
This week, I'm looking at the national debt, New York City's AI policy, paid political propaganda, Amy Acton's refusal to debate, Cuyahoga County's absurdly expensive jail, one of the best campaign ads I have seen this year and the third season of _Silo_.
Let's get into it.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bdb62bab-7574-4935-8645-44e72dc6d1ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..X1jxXXgtBEvWEalbY8oLiRZBpY70fm76wbsAC-Q9Mdc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214175682)
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..X1jxXXgtBEvWEalbY8oLiRZBpY70fm76wbsAC-Q9Mdc?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=214175682)
* * *
## Washington Is Losing Control of the Debt
Any member of Congress who is not talking seriously about the national debt and annual deficit is committing a dereliction of duty. Congress controls the power of the purse. Presidents propose budgets and sign legislation, but Congress decides what the federal government taxes, borrows and spends.
The national debt is the total amount the federal government owes after decades of borrowing. It has now crossed **$40 trillion**. The deficit is the amount the government spends beyond what it collects during a single year. The Congressional Budget Office originally projected a **$1.9 trillion deficit for fiscal year 2026** , while updated estimates have placed it closer to $2.1 trillion. Every annual deficit adds to the debt.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b379468f-a0d4-47ef-839e-a05c6c965d58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The bond market determines how expensive that borrowing becomes. When the federal government sells Treasury securities, investors are lending it money. As of September 4, the 10-year Treasury yield was around **4.8 percent** , while the 30-year yield was approximately **5.27 percent**. Inflation, Federal Reserve policy, economic growth and global demand all affect the yield rate.
The government is already spending approximately **$1 trillion annually on net interest**. As trillions of dollars in existing debt mature and are refinanced at higher rates, that burden grows. A one-percentage-point increase on $10 trillion of refinanced debt eventually means approximately another $100 billion in annual interest.
**We are paying one credit card with another credit card!**
There are only a few options for Congress:
* **Reduce deficit spending while growing the economy.** Bring annual deficits under control while expanding the economic base that supports the debt.
* **Produce budget surpluses and pay down the debt.** Go beyond reducing deficits by taking in more than the government spends and using those surpluses to actually lower the outstanding debt.
* **Inflate away the debt.** Allow inflation to make yesterday's debt easier to repay with tomorrow's less valuable dollars. This last option quietly destroys everyone's purchasing power.

Congress keeps treating this like a problem for the next election cycle. The bond market may eventually decide that Washington has run out of time.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4e1a1fbf-c233-4ce3-91c0-e3c4467cf342?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
## Banning AI From Schools Is Only Half the Solution
New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI for students from prekindergarten through eighth grade. The policy affects nearly 600,000 students.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/ec94acab-bdd2-41ff-884e-c3c72624cfe5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**My initial reaction is that this is both a good idea and a bad idea.**
Children need to learn how to write an essay, construct an outline, solve arithmetic and algebra problems, think critically and interact with other children. They should not be able to type a homework assignment into ChatGPT and submit whatever comes back. An AI system should not replace teachers, parents, reading, handwriting, problem-solving or the uncomfortable process of figuring something out.
On that point, Mamdani is right to hit pause.
However, New York City should be asking OpenAI, Anthropic and other companies to build protected systems specifically for students.
**Imagine an AI tutor that does not provide the answer.**
It asks the child questions, identifies where the child became confused and walks through the problem one step at a time. It could adjust explanations to the student's reading level, help a teacher identify patterns across a classroom and give a child extra practice at home. It would function as an extension of the teacher, not a replacement.
Nobody would object to every child having access to a responsible tutor after school. The issue is whether the technology is designed to teach or designed to complete the assignment.
South Korea is already moving toward treating AI access as public infrastructure, with plans to provide its citizens free access to premium-level domestic AI services. The United States cannot respond to this technological change by teaching wealthy children how to use AI privately while banning poorer children from encountering it in public schools.
Pause the current tools. Protect children's privacy and cognitive development.
But build, like right now, better tools. Simply banning AI and pretending it will disappear is not an education policy.
* * *
## Your Political Feed Is Being Manufactured
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3b26b662-6b2c-4062-90fc-b98baa25a5f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Illustration by _The Atlantic_. Source: servtheclipper / YouTube
_[The Atlantic](https://substack.com/redirect/c652cca3-098e-4e4f-8c91-ff50c40bb939?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ published a disturbing investigation into a political clipping operation ](https://substack.com/redirect/c652cca3-098e-4e4f-8c91-ff50c40bb939?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)called Elephant Clipping. A clipper takes a longer video, chops it into short pieces and posts those pieces across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts.
According to _The Atlantic_ , Elephant Clipping was run through a company in Latvia and recruited subcontractors, many apparently outside the United States, to post pro-Republican material. Participants could submit favorable conservative clips for payment through a reported **$300,000 monthly campaign budget** , receiving approximately $300 for every million views.
The investigation found instructions telling participants to use American proxy servers and hide their locations. The clips were posted through accounts designed to resemble ordinary Americans independently supporting Republican ideas. Some campaigns offered additional money for favorable Vivek Ramaswamy content. The identities of the ultimate funders were not disclosed. The Atlantic
This caught my attention because of the coordinated online attack against **Brian Poindexter, the Democratic candidate in Ohio 's 7th Congressional District.** Multiple conservative and Daily Wire-aligned accounts appeared to push essentially the same framing at roughly the same time.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/046558c8-e6a0-4510-8f24-0ef08e1106d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I cannot prove that those specific posts came from Elephant Clipping or any paid operation. What I can say is that the timing looked more like a coordinated distribution strategy than several people independently discovering the same **supposedly** **important** story.
This happens on both sides. Democrats use influencers, consultants, friendly publications and coordinated messaging too. The larger problem is that most people scrolling through social media cannot tell whether they are seeing journalism, advertising, campaign material or an overseas contractor being paid for views.
The media environment is bought, organized and manipulated. Your feed is not a neutral reflection of what people care about. Money decides and messages appear organic.
* * *
## Amy Acton Still Owes Ohioans a Debate
Amy Acton has declined to debate Vivek Ramaswamy, and I understand the campaign strategy. Her campaign says Ramaswamy and his billionaire supporters have spent more than $50 million on inaccurate and disgusting attacks against Acton and her family, including AI-generated material portraying her as having a substance-abuse problem.
The Angry Ohioan
[The Debate Format Is Broken. Walking Away From Voters Is Not the Answer.](https://substack.com/redirect/7baa4984-b9bb-486b-8334-28855f113353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Hey, Angry Patriots...
[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/7baa4984-b9bb-486b-8334-28855f113353?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
2 days ago * 3 likes * 4 comments * The Angry Democrat
I understand why she does not want to reward that conduct with a statewide stage.
I still think her decision is wrong.
Neither Acton nor Ramaswamy faced a primary that forced them to defend their ideas before their own parties. Republican leaders lined up behind Ramaswamy early, while Democratic power players helped clear the field for Acton whether anyone wants to call that an endorsement or not. Ohioans were left with two nominees who have never held legislative office and no voting records showing how either would govern.
Now we may not get a debate either.
[The Ohio Democratic Party condemned Mike DeWine](https://substack.com/redirect/a7024c3c-0a5a-40b2-82c7-dd141924c587?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for refusing to debate Nan Whaley in 2022. It called debates "the equivalent of a job interview" and said candidates should not avoid scrutiny, fact-checking or difficult questions because they are leading in the polls.
**That principle cannot change because the Democrat is now the candidate who sees more political risk than reward.**
This is part of a larger retreat from public access.
The Cuyahoga County Democratic Party discouraged judicial candidates from participating in [Judge4Yourself](https://substack.com/redirect/86552915-0374-4f1d-819e-3c6603cb4569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Some Republicans refuse editorial-board interviews with _cleveland.com_ and _The Plain Dealer_.
Candidates (Mike Dovilla) skip League of Women Voters forums.
Former Senator Sherrod Brown and his opponent Senator Jon Husted seemingly will not debate.
Members of Congress replace actual town halls with telephone events where questions can be screened in advance.
The public increasingly receives only campaign advertisements, curated events and consultant-approved communication.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/46bc35a3-c2d7-4fd9-ac8a-ebe49b035f72?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congressman, David Joyce, pretending to be accessible
I agree that the traditional debate format is broken. It rewards interruptions, lies and made-for-TikTok insults. Change the format. Control the microphones. Give candidates the topics beforehand. Crowdsource questions from Ohioans and fact-check claims in real time.
But do not eliminate the debate. Acton does not owe Ramaswamy a performance opportunity. She owes Ohioans the chance to compare both candidates under the same conditions.
* * *
## Stop Spending Money on This Damn Jail
Cuyahoga County's proposed Central Services Campus has become one of the most expensive correctional projects I could find anywhere in the developed world.
The Angry Ohioan
[Cuyahoga County's Nearly Billion-Dollar Jail Makes No Damn Sense](https://substack.com/redirect/60274383-9d6d-4a23-91f9-f59faf890331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Hey, Angry Patriots...
[Read more](https://substack.com/redirect/60274383-9d6d-4a23-91f9-f59faf890331?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
4 days ago * 1 like * The Angry Democrat
The current estimate is approximately **$889 million for 1,886 beds** , or roughly **$471,000 per bed**. That is about what it costs to build a very nice three- or four-bedroom suburban house for every person the jail is designed to hold.
**Where the fuck is the money going?**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9b5318d4-fc48-4b2f-9f0e-b71e41f34963?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Franklin County's completed corrections center cost approximately **$280,000 per rated bed**. It includes medical care, mental-health treatment, behavioral programming, addiction services, direct supervision and reentry support. Cuyahoga is proposing many of the same modern features at a cost approximately **68 percent higher per bed**.
Recent facilities in the United Kingdom, France and Japan have also been built for substantially less per bed. These are not cages without medical treatment, ventilation or rehabilitation services. They are modern facilities in wealthy countries.
Cuyahoga's HVAC estimate alone is approximately **$85.8 million for 872,000 square feet** , or around $98 per square foot. That is nearly twice the reported per-square-foot mechanical cost of the Coyote Ridge correctional facility and Somerset County Jail. It even exceeds the per-square-foot cost of a broader hospital mechanical package that included HVAC, plumbing and medical gas.
Yet too many Democrats would rather turn a blind eye than hold their own people accountable. They excuse bad decisions, accept mediocre governance and demand so little from the people around them because they refuse to hold themselves or their political allies to any meaningful standard.
Bullshit.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b252b27c-cd58-4d36-83fd-e8548ad41ce3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
People in jail deserve dignity, medical care and protection from abuse. Many have not been convicted of anything. None of that explains $471,000 per bed.
Cancel it if necessary. Pay a cancellation penalty.
**
I would rather lose millions stopping a financially indefensible project than obligate taxpayers to more than a billion dollars because political insiders are afraid to admit they lost control.**
* * *
## Brian Poindexter Made One of the Best Ads of 2026
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a52b2f85-147e-48ac-8384-008e091b3101?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Brian Poindexter released one of the best campaign advertisements I have seen in a long time.
The advertisement features his daughters making fun of him, from the enormous phone clipped to his belt to the little generational idiosyncrasies that start appearing when a man reaches his mid-40s and becomes fully comfortable being a goofy dad.
The ad was obviously planned and scripted, but it did not feel artificial. That is what made it work.
His daughters appeared comfortable, funny and proud of their father. Brian was willing to be the joke. The entire family seemed to understand the plot without a consultant instructing them to be a "normal" family for the camera.
That is incredibly difficult to manufacture.
Political advertising usually fails when candidates attempt to sand away everything unusual about themselves. Consultants take a real person, remove the quirks, replace normal language with approved phrases and produce another video of someone walking through a factory while pretending to listen to a worker.
## [Everybody Wants to Be Zohran Mamdani](https://substack.com/redirect/88cc28d4-2329-47af-b4b9-c5dd26f24b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/profile/102996536-the-angry-democrat)| | *
---|---|---
| Aug 19
[](https://substack.com/redirect/88cc28d4-2329-47af-b4b9-c5dd26f24b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass recently released one of the cringiest political videos I have seen in a while.](https://substack.com/redirect/88cc28d4-2329-47af-b4b9-c5dd26f24b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/88cc28d4-2329-47af-b4b9-c5dd26f24b40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Poindexter went in the opposite direction. He let voters see the oversized phone, the awkwardness and the dad humor. He made his personality part of the message.
The result also creates an unavoidable contrast with incumbent Congressman Max Miller. Miller is going through an extremely public divorce and custody battle ex-wife. She has made serious allegations against him, which Miller denies, and the legal battle has generated thousands of pages of court docs and media coverage.
Poindexter did not need to mention any of that. He showed a warm, relaxed relationship with his daughters, and voters will recognize the contrast themselves.
The best political advertisements do not tell us that a candidate is authentic. They allow us to see enough of the candidate to decide for ourselves.
**Brian 's ad did that.**
* * *
## _Silo_ Was Disappointing, and I'm Still Watching
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c949b349-e940-4884-8bcf-64e0008cdd9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Per Stensen in Silo: Trillionaire Bunker Builder 🤦🏾♂️
Finally, the third season of Apple TV's _Silo_ has ended.
_Silo_ feels like someone put _Snowpiercer_ , _The Platform_ , _Cube_ and the underground city of Zion from _The Matrix_ into a blender. It is a dystopian mystery built around class, information control, rebellion, surveillance and the question of who gets to decide what people are allowed to know.
For two seasons, it has been a good show to watch for 45 minutes at the end of the night. It is entertaining enough to keep me interested and mysterious enough to make me return for the next episode.
Season three, however, was a chore.
The story moved SOOOOOOO slow. The writing became tedious, the political parallels were painfully on the nose, and several supposedly dramatic developments were predictable. Political allegory works when it deepens a story. Here, the show sometimes appeared to stop telling its own story and started playing into Elon Musk haters.
What made the experience stranger was reading reviews that barely discussed those obvious parallels. When a show is this politically on the nose and so little of the published conversation acknowledges it, I start questioning how organic that conversation really is.
The absence of the most obvious criticism (Elon parallel) made the online discussion feel carefully managed.
I watched every episode and I will watch season fourth and final (thankfully) season.
Apparently, my disappointment has limits.
Let me know what was on your radar this week.

clean_body: National debt, AI in schools, manufactured politics, a billion-dollar jail and everything else on my radar this week. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more ? We need to find other ANGRY DEMOCRATS. Please consider sharing and subscribing to fuel the ANGER for change. National debt, AI in schools, manufactured politics, a billion-dollar jail and everything else on my radar this week. | | | Sep 5 | | | | | | | | | | | | Hey, Angry Patriots! Welcome to The Angry Files , the politics on my radar this week. This week, I'm looking at the national debt, New York City's AI policy, paid political propaganda, Amy Acton's refusal to debate, Cuyahoga County's absurdly expensive jail, one of the best campaign ads I have seen this year and the third season of Silo. Let's get into it. | | ---|---|--- Washington Is Losing Control of the Debt Any member of Congress who is not talking seriously about the national debt and annual deficit is committing a dereliction of duty. Congress controls the power of the purse. Presidents propose budgets and sign legislation, but Congress decides what the federal government taxes, borrows and spends. The national debt is the total amount the federal government owes after decades of borrowing. It has now crossed $40 trillion. The deficit is the amount the government spends beyond what it collects during a single year. The Congressional Budget Office originally projected a $1.9 trillion deficit for fiscal year 2026 , while updated estimates have placed it closer to $2.1 trillion. Every annual deficit adds to the debt. | | ---|---|--- The bond market determines how expensive that borrowing becomes. When the federal government sells Treasury securities, investors are lending it money. As of September 4, the 10-year Treasury yield was around 4.8 percent , while the 30-year yield was approximately 5.27 percent. Inflation, Federal Reserve policy, economic growth and global demand all affect the yield rate. The government is already spending approximately $1 trillion annually on net interest. As trillions of dollars in existing debt mature and are refinanced at higher rates, that burden grows. A one-percentage-point increase on $10 trillion of refinanced debt eventually means approximately another $100 billion in annual interest. We are paying one credit card with another credit card! There are only a few options for Congress: Reduce deficit spending while growing the economy. Bring annual deficits under control while expanding the economic base that supports the debt. Produce budget surpluses and pay down the debt. Go beyond reducing deficits by taking in more than the government spends and using those surpluses to actually lower the outstanding debt. Inflate away the debt. Allow inflation to make yesterday's debt easier to repay with tomorrow's less valuable dollars. This last option quietly destroys everyone's purchasing power. Congress keeps treating this like a problem for the next election cycle. The bond market may eventually decide that Washington has run out of time. Banning AI From Schools Is Only Half the Solution New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced a one-year moratorium on student-facing generative AI for students from prekindergarten through eighth grade. The policy affects nearly 600,000 students. My initial reaction is that this is both a good idea and a bad idea. Children need to learn how to write an essay, construct an outline, solve arithmetic and algebra problems, think critically and interact with other children. They should not be able to type a homework assignment into ChatGPT and submit whatever comes back. An AI system should not replace teachers, parents, reading, handwriting, problem-solving or the uncomfortable process of figuring something out. On that point, Mamdani is right to hit pause. However, New York City should be asking OpenAI, Anthropic and other companies to build protected systems specifically for students. Imagine an AI tutor that does not provide the answer. It asks the child questions, identifies where the child became confused and walks through the problem one step at a time. It could adjust explanations to the student's reading level, help a teacher identify patterns across a classroom and give a child extra practice at home. It would function as an extension of the teacher, not a replacement. Nobody would object to every child having access to a responsible tutor after school. The issue is whether the technology is designed to teach or designed to complete the assignment. South Korea is already moving toward treating AI access as public infrastructure, with plans to provide its citizens free access to premium-level domestic AI services. The United States cannot respond to this technological change by teaching wealthy children how to use AI privately while banning poorer children from encountering it in public schools. Pause the current tools. Protect children's privacy and cognitive development. But build, like right now, better tools. Simply banning AI and pretending it will disappear is not an education policy. Your Political Feed Is Being Manufactured | | ---|---|--- Illustration by The Atlantic. Source: servtheclipper / YouTube Elephant Clipping. A clipper takes a longer video, chops it into short pieces and posts those pieces across TikTok, Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts. According to The Atlantic , Elephant Clipping was run through a company in Latvia and recruited subcontractors, many apparently outside the United States, to post pro-Republican material. Participants could submit favorable conservative clips for payment through a reported $300,000 monthly campaign budget , receiving approximately $300 for every million views. The investigation found instructions telling participants to use American proxy servers and hide their locations. The clips were posted through accounts designed to resemble ordinary Americans independently supporting Republican ideas. Some campaigns offered additional money for favorable Vivek Ramaswamy content. The identities of the ultimate funders were not disclosed. The Atlantic This caught my attention because of the coordinated online attack against Brian Poindexter, the Democratic candidate in Ohio 's 7th Congressional District. Multiple conservative and Daily Wire-aligned accounts appeared to push essentially the same framing at roughly the same time. | | ---|---|--- I cannot prove that those specific posts came from Elephant Clipping or any paid operation. What I can say is that the timing looked more like a coordinated distribution strategy than several people independently discovering the same supposedly important story. This happens on both sides. Democrats use influencers, consultants, friendly publications and coordinated messaging too. The larger problem is that most people scrolling through social media cannot tell whether they are seeing journalism, advertising, campaign material or an overseas contractor being paid for views. The media environment is bought, organized and manipulated. Your feed is not a neutral reflection of what people care about. Money decides and messages appear organic. Amy Acton Still Owes Ohioans a Debate Amy Acton has declined to debate Vivek Ramaswamy, and I understand the campaign strategy. Her campaign says Ramaswamy and his billionaire supporters have spent more than $50 million on inaccurate and disgusting attacks against Acton and her family, including AI-generated material portraying her as having a substance-abuse problem. The Angry Ohioan Hey, Angry Patriots... 2 days ago 3 likes 4 comments The Angry Democrat I understand why she does not want to reward that conduct with a statewide stage. I still think her decision is wrong. Neither Acton nor Ramaswamy faced a primary that forced them to defend their ideas before their own parties. Republican leaders lined up behind Ramaswamy early, while Democratic power players helped clear the field for Acton whether anyone wants to call that an endorsement or not. Ohioans were left with two nominees who have never held legislative office and no voting records showing how either would govern. Now we may not get a debate either. for refusing to debate Nan Whaley in 2022. It called debates "the equivalent of a job interview" and said candidates should not avoid scrutiny, fact-checking or difficult questions because they are leading in the polls. That principle cannot change because the Democrat is now the candidate who sees more political risk than reward. This is part of a larger retreat from public access. The Cuyahoga County Democratic Party discouraged judicial candidates from participating in . Some Republicans refuse editorial-board interviews with cleveland.com and The Plain Dealer. Candidates (Mike Dovilla) skip League of Women Voters forums. Former Senator Sherrod Brown and his opponent Senator Jon Husted seemingly will not debate. Members of Congress replace actual town halls with telephone events where questions can be screened in advance. The public increasingly receives only campaign advertisements, curated events and consultant-approved communication. | | ---|---|--- Congressman, David Joyce, pretending to be accessible I agree that the traditional debate format is broken. It rewards interruptions, lies and made-for-TikTok insults. Change the format. Control the microphones. Give candidates the topics beforehand. Crowdsource questions from Ohioans and fact-check claims in real time. But do not eliminate the debate. Acton does not owe Ramaswamy a performance opportunity. She owes Ohioans the chance to compare both candidates under the same conditions. Stop Spending Money on This Damn Jail Cuyahoga County's proposed Central Services Campus has become one of the most expensive correctional projects I could find anywhere in the developed world. The Angry Ohioan Hey, Angry Patriots... 4 days ago 1 like The Angry Democrat The current estimate is approximately $889 million for 1,886 beds , or roughly $471,000 per bed. That is about what it costs to build a very nice three- or four-bedroom suburban house for every person the jail is designed to hold. Where the fuck is the money going? | | ---|---|--- Franklin County's completed corrections center cost approximately $280,000 per rated bed. It includes medical care, mental-health treatment, behavioral programming, addiction services, direct supervision and reentry support. Cuyahoga is proposing many of the same modern features at a cost approximately 68 percent higher per bed. Recent facilities in the United Kingdom, France and Japan have also been built for substantially less per bed. These are not cages without medical treatment, ventilation or rehabilitation services. They are modern facilities in wealthy countries. Cuyahoga's HVAC estimate alone is approximately $85.8 million for 872,000 square feet , or around $98 per square foot. That is nearly twice the reported per-square-foot mechanical cost of the Coyote Ridge correctional facility and Somerset County Jail. It even exceeds the per-square-foot cost of a broader hospital mechanical package that included HVAC, plumbing and medical gas. Yet too many Democrats would rather turn a blind eye than hold their own people accountable. They excuse bad decisions, accept mediocre governance and demand so little from the people around them because they refuse to hold themselves or their political allies to any meaningful standard. Bullshit. | | ---|---|--- People in jail deserve dignity, medical care and protection from abuse. Many have not been convicted of anything. None of that explains $471,000 per bed. Cancel it if necessary. Pay a cancellation penalty. I would rather lose millions stopping a financially indefensible project than obligate taxpayers to more than a billion dollars because political insiders are afraid to admit they lost control. Brian Poindexter Made One of the Best Ads of 2026 Brian Poindexter released one of the best campaign advertisements I have seen in a long time. The advertisement features his daughters making fun of him, from the enormous phone clipped to his belt to the little generational idiosyncrasies that start appearing when a man reaches his mid-40s and becomes fully comfortable being a goofy dad. The ad was obviously planned and scripted, but it did not feel artificial. That is what made it work. His daughters appeared comfortable, funny and proud of their father. Brian was willing to be the joke. The entire family seemed to understand the plot without a consultant instructing them to be a "normal" family for the camera. That is incredibly difficult to manufacture. Political advertising usually fails when candidates attempt to sand away everything unusual about themselves. Consultants take a real person, remove the quirks, replace normal language with approved phrases and produce another video of someone walking through a factory while pretending to listen to a worker. | | | | ---|---|--- | Aug 19 | Poindexter went in the opposite direction. He let voters see the oversized phone, the awkwardness and the dad humor. He made his personality part of the message. The result also creates an unavoidable contrast with incumbent Congressman Max Miller. Miller is going through an extremely public divorce and custody battle ex-wife. She has made serious allegations against him, which Miller denies, and the legal battle has generated thousands of pages of court docs and media coverage. Poindexter did not need to mention any of that. He showed a warm, relaxed relationship with his daughters, and voters will recognize the contrast themselves. The best political advertisements do not tell us that a candidate is authentic. They allow us to see enough of the candidate to decide for ourselves. Brian 's ad did that. Silo Was Disappointing, and I'm Still Watching | | ---|---|--- Per Stensen in Silo: Trillionaire Bunker Builder 🤦🏾♂️ Finally, the third season of Apple TV's Silo has ended. Silo feels like someone put Snowpiercer , The Platform , Cube and the underground city of Zion from The Matrix into a blender. It is a dystopian mystery built around class, information control, rebellion, surveillance and the question of who gets to decide what people are allowed to know. For two seasons, it has been a good show to watch for 45 minutes at the end of the night. It is entertaining enough to keep me interested and mysterious enough to make me return for the next episode. Season three, however, was a chore. The story moved SOOOOOOO slow. The writing became tedious, the political parallels were painfully on the nose, and several supposedly dramatic developments were predictable. Political allegory works when it deepens a story. Here, the show sometimes appeared to stop telling its own story and started playing into Elon Musk haters. What made the experience stranger was reading reviews that barely discussed those obvious parallels. When a show is this politically on the nose and so little of the published conversation acknowledges it, I start questioning how organic that conversation really is. The absence of the most obvious criticism (Elon parallel) made the online discussion feel carefully managed. I watched every episode and I will watch season fourth and final (thankfully) season. Apparently, my disappointment has limits. Let me know what was on your radar this week. Stay Angry. Join otherANGRY DEMOCRATS** by supporting Matt's work. My dad needs your help
My dad needs your help.

| | | | Peter, It's hard to watch someone you love get viciously attacked every hour on TV. So today, I'm breaking my silence. **My name is Mattie (Paxton) Hayworth, and I 'm the proud daughter of Ken Paxton - the Republican nominee for U.S. Senate in Texas.** Before the Left spends another dollar trying to tear down my dad, I want you to hear from someone who _actually_ knows him. My dad was the one who led me to Christ. He was the kind of dad who made you feel seen and loved. He showed up to my games and school events - present in the moments that mattered and in the quiet, ordinary ones too. The Left wants you to believe he's Public Enemy #1. But to me, he's simply **_" Dad."_**

The eternal flame at Kennedy’s grave is going to be in Trump’s shadow if this arch gets built.
#
Peter:
We’ve always known that the Arc de Trump would put Arlington National Cemetery in shadow.
We’ve also been confident the arch would put graves of fallen U.S. service members in shadow.
So, we decided to figure out the actual extent of that. Here’s what we found:
[](https://act.votevets.org/go/2927?c0=vv-pac-em-sep26.f1bOKp&refcode=em260905-1-180&t=1&akid=35541%2E3013755%2EHfZNmU)
That arch won’t just put our honored dead in shadow. It will overshadow the final resting places of John F. Kennedy, his wife Jackie, their daughter Arabella, and his brothers, Bobby and Ted.
Think about that.
The eternal flame at Kennedy’s grave is going to be in Trump’s shadow if this arch gets built. The grave of a man who volunteered to serve his country at war and risked his life chasing down Japanese ships in a patrol torpedo boat. Who put the life jacket strap of one of his wounded crewmates in his mouth and swam three miles to safety in shark infested waters. Who was assassinated by a sniper’s bullet at the age of 46.
The Arc de Trump would put his grave in shadow, and who knows how many others.
The Secretary of the Interior just announced they plan to break ground on that arch in the next two weeks. The National Capital Planning Commission hasn’t even voted on final approval for that arch, and won’t until October. Trump wants to force this through before anyone can stop him.
But VoteVets will fight him every step of the way, and we need your help.

A proposed federal film tax credit has united union crews, populist Republicans, and California Democrats -- while Tennessee quietly built the playbook that could land Paramount
An unlikely alliance is forming around a federal film production tax credit, and it was on full display this week in a single chain of social media posts.
On September 1, Teamsters General President Sean O'Brien thanked President Trump for "prioritizing passage of a federal film tax credit." Rep. Tim Burchett (R-TN) quote-posted O'Brien with the tag line "Let's make Hollywood great again," tagging both the president and the union. Then Spencer Pratt -- the former reality TV star turned acerbic commentator on Los Angeles politics -- layered on a manifesto of his own, arguing that a federal credit would scatter production away from Hollywood and seed a "regional film renaissance" in places like Nashville, Atlanta, Austin, Lexington, and Billings.
"The more film productions & crews we have marinating in places like TN, the less woke their films will be," Pratt wrote, claiming a "tremendously underserved market of 100 million normal Americans" alienated by recent Hollywood output. "The more decentralized the film industry becomes, the better the variety of entertainment offerings there will be."

| | Friend,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...

---
**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Friend, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

The question is whether it's enough.

Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America...

They're not the majority. _They 're the exception. _

They're the ones willing to take the heat.

The ones willing to stand alone.

The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: _" I love this country." _
---
[](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=4cb8c1b7782a4a13ae8f717a4cba07da&_e=KTDrZ15g76UTj18YGc7Qb62Xo5Wbi6pvzm-ALwGnJDxpTfFquU_0NNcW7mju6WfmWuEvXQZzLncKwnpkp-jkLiuUcSZO5GWBT4NdsDPD38GU8FZmx6jeSmRsQISVJpbksMcglxgKirg0-xOnnjv-_5opVDT5Yuk8uUqubNbk0OdPaPajxtzK1pnjx6YVIKnH-yJLjSvHW7l2zcvzpTb24EAQk8IJQe1NnLBRxVHh9wfu3RICJzETfO2p5t3Bn6w9_Bxv32EoZfR1svcZ00YUhiehXRI4p8KTzzioR_UpdJQkroHfFSn7zuE7w4CsNYeevr02xX8Gu9B4sRXRi_FOvA5w2bZclUBqzzOdISSwJZ5_j0FtTDXL8tFVTxqdYZn4UCpX3PCOe09yscwDHs--L6SHYHUl0LA2mlXkoNz7RIqU9HUQDxZmTh1C9VOe8vHqNxx7EwdzdJspQpLjbXt-Vh8hp6N2Wv5Bt76D2W0GD1PtTFhj_xnYBcw5XGUzFrmERpOl8DEVmOxhZHcHJedkAGho1ox6_3trJiSbdfy3YJYer0d9Z-rhwkvSXOy6h7i5yACzwEP-VoiN3HDPT3wRnWg-qgfKmXRIfANIWgFjXeGeKT7pAlTedQqYiXRnOW_TcwGFovNQiICiD05vELK_MdlITvQsbtYxWw_pJTVncLC-rBcaZMYnL3lHNtRvoYsRzLvKM5el3DM-aDk0BPN5umnrBE8F_oVXtrfYbVzk8A8%3D)

And every time one of those students raises their hand...

We have a choice.

Back them. _Or leave them on their own. _

**Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. **

Everything they need to actually stand their ground.

Not symbolically. For real.

They've already made the decision to lead.

All they're waiting on... is you and me.

**Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. **

clean_body: Meanwhile, my opponent wants to defund ICE | Friend, I will always back our men and women in Blue. But don’t take my word for it. I just received an endorsement from the Arkansas Narcotic Officers Association. They work tirelessly to keep dangerous drugs off our streets and away from our children. My Radical Opponent, however, actively wants to flood our streets with drugs. Hallie Shoffner continues to double down on her stance to DEFUND ICE. If we don’t have ICE, drug cartels rush through the southern border and smuggle drugs, human slaves, and guns into America. And of course, those drugs wind up taken by our children, victims are extorted in the Black Market human trafficking ring, and guns end up in the hands of violent gangs and criminals. Hallie Shoffner wants all of that for America, simply because she thinks illegal immigrants should face zero consequences. And if she pulls off a miracle and beats me, we’ll be thrown right back into the Biden/Harris immigration system, when our borders were wide open, the cartels feared nothing, and American citizens suffered. | In Service, Tom Cotton | | PAID FOR BY TOM COTTON FOR SENATE Copyright (C) 2026 Tom Cotton for Senate, All rights reserved.

Dear Friend, We can flip this seat. I believe that more today than I did when we started this campaign. Everywhere I go across Southwestern Pennsylvania, I meet Democrats, Republicans, and Independents who are frustrated with Washington and ready for something different. But believing we can win isn't enough. **We have to do the work it takes to win -- and we need your help now.** Election Day is getting closer, and there are still thousands of voters across PA-14 who need to hear about our campaign and why I'm running. We need volunteers knocking doors, making phone calls, writing postcards, helping at events, and reaching voters in every corner of this district. But there's one thing every one of us can do: **talk to the people we already know.** Talk to your friends. Talk to your neighbors. Talk to your family and coworkers. Make sure they know who I am, why I'm running, and what I stand for. A conversation with someone they know and trust can mean more than another piece of mail or another political ad. We have a tool to make that easier. We've built the organization. We have volunteers across the district who believe this race is worth the work. **Now is the time to turn that belief into action.** If you want to flip this seat, help us do the work it takes to make it happen. Knock a door. Make a call. Write a postcard. **And before this weekend is over, talk to five people you know about why you 're supporting this campaign.** **We can win PA-14. # [Why I'm a Michigan Democrat](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=214303522&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjE0MzAzNTIyLCJpYXQiOjE3ODg2MTg1MTIsImV4cCI6MTc5MTIxMDUxMiwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.xFbFtW0QCXigvKku9gj_wFbwpF8rhKV3_NNoPMalqU0)

---

Let's get something straight.
I'm a Michigan Democrat.
And Michigan taught me something important: capitalism and labor aren't enemies. They built this state together.
One person has an idea. Another puts up the capital. Somebody builds the factory. Somebody runs the line. Somebody wires the building, fits the pipe, machines the part, designs the engine.
And eventually something rolls out the door that people want to buy.
Michigan's history is a story of enterprise and labor sharing the same factory floor.
That's capitalism.
Michigan knows something about it.
And I believe in it.
I believe in **labor, capitalism, and democracy** , because each one keeps the others honest.
The problem with capitalism isn't that people can build companies, make money, accumulate wealth, or succeed.
Good. I want them to succeed.
I want entrepreneurs. I want investors. I want competition. I want somebody sitting in a garage with an idea everyone else thinks is crazy, convinced they can build the next great American company.
The problem comes when economic power becomes so concentrated that the people doing the work have no power of their own.
And the answer to that isn't socialism.
It's organized labor.
That distinction matters.
A strong labor movement doesn't ask the government to own the factory.
It gives the people working in the factory enough power to sit across the table from the people who own it and negotiate.
That's not socialism.
That's bargaining.
That's capitalism with a counterweight.
The electrician matters.
The pipefitter matters.
The machinist matters.
The engineer matters.
And when those workers organize for better wages, safer workplaces, health care, retirement, and a fair share of the value they helped create, they aren't overthrowing capitalism.
**They 're participating in it.**
Michigan helped prove this can work.
A company can make money.
An investor can earn a return.
An entrepreneur can become wealthy.
And a worker can earn a good wage, buy a home, raise a family, send a kid to college, and retire with dignity.
Those things are not contradictions.
That's the bargain.
And I reject this idea that America has to choose between an economy dominated by corporations and an economy dominated by government.
I don't want either one.
I don't want government deciding which company deserves to succeed or how much ambition is allowed to earn.
And I don't want a handful of corporations becoming so powerful that the people who work for them have no meaningful ability to negotiate.
I want markets.
I want competition.
I want capital.
And I want labor strong enough to meet capital across the table as an equal.
Because profit isn't a dirty word.
Profit can mean you built something people value.
Wealth can mean you took a risk and it paid off.
Success should be celebrated.
But success carries obligations.
If thousands of people get up every morning and help make your company prosper, they deserve bargaining power and a meaningful share of the prosperity they helped create.
That's my alternative to socialism.
Not less capitalism.
**Better capitalism.**
And Michigan should be at the center of building it.
I want us making the next generation of cars, batteries, semiconductors, defense systems, medical equipment, and advanced technology.
I want cranes in the sky and factories opening instead of closing.
I want entrepreneurs starting companies here.
I want companies investing here.
I want apprentices learning trades here.
I want union halls full.
And I want the jobs created by all that growth to be jobs you can actually build a life around.
That requires capital.
It requires people willing to risk it.
And it requires organized labor strong enough to make sure prosperity doesn't stop at the executive suite.
That's the balance.
So I'm not interested in choosing between being pro-business and pro-worker.
That's a false choice.
I'm interested in successful businesses creating successful workers.
I'm not interested in tearing capitalism down because it hasn't always lived up to its promise.
I want to make it live up to its promise.
Build things in Michigan.
Create good-paying union jobs.
Grow American manufacturing.
Reward the people who take risks.
Respect the people whose labor turns those risks into something real.
Let businesses compete.
Let workers organize.
Let people succeed.
And let's build an economy where prosperity isn't handed down from Washington or hoarded in a corporate boardroom, but created by millions of Americans who have the freedom to build, the freedom to work, and enough power to bargain with each other.
Call it capitalism.
Call it the Michigan model.
I just call it America.
And I think it's worth building again.

Meet Joe Males:

**Joe Males is a Marine Veteran, small business-owner, city council member, and most importantly, a father. Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission.

Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved.

Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same.

Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy.

During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met.

Throughout his life, he has put service to his community at the forefront of his life’s mission. Shortly after turning 18, Joe enlisted in the Marine Corps. He attended boot camp in Camp Pendleton and later served overseas in the Philippines and Guam. After being discharged as a Sergeant, Joe remained committed to supporting his fellow veterans. He took on leadership roles in his local Elks Lodge and American Legion post, working to ensure veterans in the community had the resources and support they deserved. Following his time in the Marine Corps, Joe carried his strong work ethic and discipline into the field of computer networking services. He started in an entry-level position, worked his way through multiple leadership roles, and in 1996, he built his own business from the ground up. Joe knows firsthand the hard work and sacrifice of this journey, and he’s determined to make it easier for hardworking Americans to do the same. Joe’s entry into politics was deeply personal. After his son, a Marine who followed in his footsteps, was tragically murdered back home, Joe vowed that no parent should have to endure such a loss. Determined to take a stand for public safety and the rule of law, he ran for Hemet City Council to help ensure no other family would experience the same tragedy. During his tenure on the City Council, Joe has led numerous initiatives to improve infrastructure, drive business growth, and keep neighborhoods safe and clean. He takes pride in his ability to collaborate with fellow council members and get results, even when facing different perspectives. Joe is committed to bringing this same results-driven approach to Washington D.C., to ensure the voices of the American people are heard and their needs are met. # **It happened again?! Illinois mother charged with murder after 2-year-old found dead**

---|---|---

* **Investigators noted Walsh had recently followed the Lindsay Clancy murder trial closely,** discussing it with friends hours before her son's death, which occurred as that jury was deliberating. Walsh remains hospitalized, with prosecutors seeking to deny her pretrial release once she's transferred to jail.

Greg Casar, plans to introduce legislation **[banning artificial superintelligence](https://substack.com/redirect/b0fd80c0-2e3f-4f46-b016-ae95ce22217f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and temporarily pausing development of other advanced AI systems until a new federal regulator establishes safety rules, comparing violation penalties to those for illegally developing nuclear weapons.

body:
News, events, and action items to keep Nebraska red and growing strong.
| | | | |
---
| Letter from the Chair
---
| Fellow Nebraska Republicans,
Time for the rubber to meet the road
Today we are 59 days from the November 3 election and 24 days from the first early ballots hitting mailboxes.
That is not a calendar note. That is a deadline.
Are you knocking doors? Making calls? Putting out yard signs? Giving? Volunteering with a campaign? If the answer is "someone else will," that someone else may not show up.
Republicans have a record to run on. Democrats would rather you forget it. Here is what changed after 2024--and what would have been different if they had won.
A sovereign border again. Catch-and-release is over. The Trump administration has reported month after month of zero Border Patrol releases at the southwest border, and illegal crossings have collapsed from the Biden-era surge.
Illegal immigration in reverse. The best current household-survey analysis shows the foreign-born population down about 2.9 million since January 2025, with the illegal population down an estimated 2.3 million. Net migration turned negative--the first time in decades. That is not a talking point. That is a country taking itself back.
Safer streets. FBI data show violent crime dropped about 9-10 percent in 2025, the largest one-year decline since national estimates began in the 1930s. The murder rate fell to 4.1 per 100,000, tying the mid-1950s low.
Tax relief that stuck. The One Big Beautiful Bill locked in the 2017 tax cuts, kept the larger standard deduction, and strengthened the Child Tax Credit. It also created new relief for tips, overtime, and seniors. That is money in the pockets of working families--not another D.C. lecture about "paying their fair share.
Fraud is being aggressively pursued. The Justice Department created a Fraud Division to handle multi-agency and multi-district cases targeting government programs, benefits, and private victims. Vice President JD Vance chairs the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud in programs run jointly with states.
Rebuilding in America again. Companies have announced trillions of dollars in U.S. investment. The point is simple: more factories, more energy, more medicines made here--not in countries that do not wish us well.
Trade moving our way. Through July, the U.S. goods-and-services trade deficit is down nearly 30 percent from the same stretch in 2025. The agricultural deficit is being cut sharply from last year's blowout. USTR recently said the ag deficit was a little over $15 billion Jan-July 2026, versus a much larger 2025 gap of $44 billion. American farmers should not have to subsidize other countries' markets.
Energy dominance. Production and exports are at historic strength. The center of gravity is the Gulf of America, not the Persian Gulf. The United States is producing more liquid energy than China and Russia combined. That is national security with a paycheck attached.
Nuclear is back. After four decades of "no new nuclear", America is restarting plants, financing new reactors, and putting advanced designs through real tests. Cheap, reliable power is how you reduce energy costs and win the AI and manufacturing race.
Voters--not bureaucrats--are in charge. The Supreme Court has broken the old model of "independent" agencies and unelected bureaucrats that answered to no one. The federal workforce is down sharply including the civilian executive workforce being the lowest in 60 years. Unelected staffers do not get a veto over elections.
Parents first. The Education Freedom Tax Credit is the first nationwide federal school-choice scholarship tax credit for states that opt in. Trump Accounts give children a stake in America's future, including a $1,000 federal seed for eligible newborns.
Common sense restored. DEI is out of the federal government and merit-based is back. The Hyde Amendment and Mexico City Policy are being enforced so American taxpayers do not have to pay for abortions. The United States government again recognizes two sexes: male and female. Taxpayers are no longer underwriting the chemical and surgical sterilization of children.
Strength abroad. NATO allies are being told to pay more for their own defense. Chinese influence is being pushed out of the Panama Canal, Venezuela, and Cuba. America has used leverage to force ceasefires and settlements in eight conflicts spanning four continents that other administrations ignored or tolerated for decades.
A serious military. The recruiting crisis is over and a warrior ethos restored. Young Americans are joining again in droves. Golden Dome--the first serious nationwide missile shield of its kind--has been launched and funded.
That is the contrast. Open borders or a country. Record crime or record drops. Tax hikes or tax cuts. Weakness or peace through strength.
None of it holds if we stay home in November.
Do something this week. Pick a campaign. Take a turf list. Write a check. Put a sign in the yard. Take a neighbor to early vote when ballots drop.
Fifty-nine days. The other side is not taking a break. Neither should we.
Onward to November. Together We Win!
In Liberty and in Truth,
Mary Jane Truemper Chairman, Nebraska Republican Party

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. In his first term as Senator, Tommy was one of eight Republicans to vote against certifying the 2020 election, has been a strong pro-life advocate, and called out Democrats for being pro-crime.

Now, Coach Tuberville is running for Governor so he can continue representing Alabamians and Americans in his homestate of Alabama. The Radical Left thinks they can flip Alabama blue and turn it into the California of the South. Can he count on your support? _

Power, Prosperity, Peace
| Dear Supporters, We have just seventy hours until Primary Day! It's not much time and yet in a campaign, each day holds so much opportunity. Our campaign and [Karishma Manzur](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/17zEzBJs1PiZO7cwpZgMv7BDscQevciT/click?signature=39853d569ddb5b0c09cc30b2edae5d1e43fc7997&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.karishmaforsenate.com%2F)'s campaign are canvassing together! If you would like to participate, you can sign up to do so [here on Karishma's website](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/17zEzBJs1PiZO7cwpZgMv7BDscQevciT/click?signature=3a098de3f1607073ff40467e55cd97017014fa88&url=https%3A%2F%2Fkarishma-for-senate.solidarity.tech%2Fcanvassing). Scroll down under "**In Person Events** " on the lefthand side of the screen to find the town and time that works for you! Please note the following towns are in Paige's district: **Concord, Lebanon, Hanover, Claremont and Nashua**.
* * *
At Team Paige, we will continue our organizing and outreach. We are doing everything we can to get the word out that New Hampshire has the chance to send a working person to Washington. Paige is maximizing every minute of these final days to reach more Granite Staters. To stay updated on Paige's whereabouts, please check our [events page](https://www.solidarity.tech/ahoy/messages/17zEzBJs1PiZO7cwpZgMv7BDscQevciT/click?signature=f446fbe485169dc04d86842f88bfc928b675f074&url=https%3A%2F%2Fpaige-for-congress.solidarity.tech%2Fevents).
* * *

Fourteen years ago this month, delegates at the Democratic National Convention audibly booed as the party restored the words "God" and "Jerusalem" to its platform. The moment was dismissed as a one-night embarrassment. It was, in fact, an early warning. Since 2012, anti-Israel sentiment -- and with it antisemitism -- has moved from the margins of the Democratic coalition toward its center, culminating in the events in Michigan this week, where the state's Jewish attorney general declined to attend her own party's nominating convention because she fears for her safety there.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5e4bc25f-64da-44e4-8013-dd15f19c5059?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**Charlotte, 2012: The Warning Flare**
On September 5, 2012, in Charlotte, North Carolina, convention chairman Antonio Villaraigosa was forced to call a voice vote three times to reinstate language naming Jerusalem as Israel's capital and affirming God-given rights. Each time, boos drowned out the ayes; President Obama had personally ordered the language restored. Villaraigosa overruled the floor and declared the amendment passed over jeers. Party leaders called it an oversight corrected. The delegates' reaction -- captured on national television -- was better read as a signal of the coalition to come.
**2016 -2019: Normalization**
The pattern hardened through the decade. In 2016, leaked Democratic National Committee emails forced chairwoman Debbie Wasserman Schultz's resignation; among them were messages from party staff scheming to use Bernie Sanders's Jewish faith against him, even questioning whether he was "Jewish at all." In 2019, Representative Ilhan Omar tweeted that American support for Israel was "all about the Benjamins," invoking the centuries-old canard of Jewish financial control; a House resolution originally drafted to condemn antisemitism was diluted into a generic condemnation of "hate" that named no one. Each episode ended without consequence, teaching the party's left flank that antisemitic rhetoric carried no political price.

subject: [DEADLINE] One month left to register in Texas
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Voto Latino
body:
Millions of eligible voters across Texas are at risk of being turned away at the polls. We need to fight back.
#
Peter,
**We are officially one month away from Texas’s voter registration deadline on October 5th.**
And right now, eligible voters across the state are at risk of being turned away at the polls.
**Texas Republicans have silently scrubbed more than 1.2 million Texans from the voter rolls, meaning _over a million people could be blocked from casting a ballot in November without even knowing it._**
[**Peter, will you rush a donation to help us fight back in Texas and make sure no eligible voter is silenced by these voter purges?**](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260905-1.tSDR6W&amount=3&refcode=em20260905-553&t=1&akid=553%2E1366028%2EmfNPUa)
Texas Republicans are engaging in _massive and widespread_ voter suppression efforts because they see the writing on the wall: **James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa are on the brink of flipping Texas’ U.S. Senate seat and defeating entrenched GOP Governor Gregg Abbott.**
Peter, what we do right now will decide if Texas Republicans get away with disenfranchising millions of voters for their own political gain.
That’s why Voto Latino is on the ground in critical districts and college campuses across Texas right now helping eligible voters navigate the registration process, verify their registration status, and restore their standing before the deadline closes.
**But we’re counting on a surge of grassroots support right now to power this work.**
**[Will you chip in $3 to power our on-the-ground registration drives and make sure every eligible voter in Texas is registered before October 5th? Every single voter we register before October 5th brings us one step closer to real change for Texans.](https://act.votolatino.org/go/57?c0=em-ms-voto-20260905-1.tSDR6W&amount=3&refcode=em20260905-553&t=2&akid=553%2E1366028%2EmfNPUa)**

Thank you,
Voto Latino

Dear Friend of Life, **It can cost the abortion industry as little as $5 to get in front of a woman searching online for abortion pills.** That should stop us in our tracks. Imagine a woman who has just discovered she is pregnant. She wasn't expecting this. She may be worried about money, insurance, child care, or how she could possibly have this baby. She is frightened, overwhelmed, and looking for someone to tell her what to do next. So she reaches for her phone. Within moments, she can find an abortion provider ready to sell her pills that will end her pregnancy and the life of her baby--all without ever walking into an abortion facility. **But what if she found hope instead?** PreBorn! is a Christian ministry dedicated to saving babies from abortion and seeing lives transformed through the gospel of Jesus Christ. Our Network Clinics across America provide free ultrasounds to women facing unexpected pregnancies. When a mother has the opportunity to see her baby and hear the heartbeat, what once felt like an impossible situation can suddenly look very different. But the way women are making decisions about abortion has changed. **Approximately 70% of abortions now happen through abortion pills.** Today, we cannot simply wait and hope a frightened mother walks through the doors of a pregnancy clinic. If women are going online looking for abortion, **we have to reach them there --and we have to reach them first.** That is why PreBorn! is expanding our reach through our Virtual Care System. Through this innovative approach, we can reach women while they are looking online for answers and create an opportunity for them to connect with something profoundly different from the abortion industry: **A real person who cares about her and her baby.** A registered nurse can listen to what she is facing without judgment, answer her questions, provide pregnancy education, help identify the pressures influencing her decision, and connect her with a local PreBorn! Network Clinic where she can receive an ultrasound and continued support. And when welcomed, our nurses can pray with these women and offer them the eternal hope of Jesus Christ. [1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

In case you missed it, our Executive Director Alexandra Rojas was recently
on Democracy Now! discussing how Justice Democrats is fighting to
transform the Democratic Party and build power for the working class.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260905.kkRSyj&refcode=em20260905-38235&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=38235%2E1203867%2ErRF_Rl ]Still from Democracy Now! broadcast, with host on the left screen and
Alexandra on the right screen

Alexandra made it clear — from DSA to Justice Dems — our movement is
united around one key goal: “We are ruthlessly focused on building power
for working people.”

Unlike the establishment, we don’t answer to billionaire megadonors or
corporate interests. We punch above our weight by targeting congressional
races — challenging Do-Nothing Democratic incumbents right where our
party's core base is — and electing leaders who will finally put them
first.

Because we refuse to take a single cent from corporate PACs, our underdog
campaigns depend entirely on this grassroots team. [ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260905.kkRSyj&refcode=em20260905-38235&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=38235%2E1203867%2ErRF_Rl ]If you’re ready to
help us keep up the fight for working families, pitch in $5
right now to fuel our movement.

One thing we know for sure is that the Democratic Party has broken the
public’s trust. As we watch the corporate takeover of our country and face
an authoritarian administration, “we can either choose to be a party that
fights like hell for working people or surrender our country to white
supremacy and fascists.”

That’s why Justice Democrats does things differently,
Peter. We find and recruit
ordinary, working-class people to ascend to the highest levels of power in
Congress. By pairing local organizing power with our experience running
campaigns against tens of millions in corporate cash, we deliver real,

By Illinois Review

The surveillance video showing Lyons Township Clerk Elyse Hoffenberg and Bridgeview Mayor Steven Landek kissing inside her government office after hours has now become the most-watched video in Illinois Review history.

More than 1.6 million people have viewed the video across Illinois Review’s Facebook and X accounts, an extraordinary reach for a story that began as a local political controversy in Lyons Township.

And the audience has expanded far beyond Illinois.

The story has since been picked up by the New York Post, Daily Mail, Hindustan Times, The Times of India and Barstool Sports, giving the controversy national and international exposure.

name: Ruben Gallego for Arizona
subject: What’s a US Senator look like?
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Gallego for Arizona
body:
Ruben might not look like the rest of the Senate, but he looks a hell of a lot like the people he represents.
#

Peter —
What’s a United States Senator look like?
Let’s start with age. The median age of a Senator is 66 right now. Chuck Grassley is the oldest at 92, and he’s been in the Senate for more than 45 years.
Median wealth of a Senator? $4.4 million.
20 Senators are veterans — if you’re keeping score, that’s 20 out of 100.
Only seven of those veterans served in the War on Terror.
Each of them was a commissioned officer — except Ruben Gallego.
Ruben Gallego was a grunt, and served in combat in Iraq. He had to fight through the system to get his VA benefits when he came home.
Ruben is not a millionaire. He’s got three young kids. He’s 45 years old, which is literally the same amount of time Chuck Grassley has been serving in the Senate.
Both of his parents were immigrants, and he was raised by a single mother on a secretary’s salary with his three sisters.
Ruben might not look like the rest of the Senate, but he looks a hell of a lot like the people he represents. He had to fight every step of the way to get there, but he’s brought that fight to the United States Senate.
If you ask us, that’s a good thing. Something we need a little more of.
If you agree, we’re asking you:
[**Add your name and tell Ruben you have his back. If we want to fix Congress, we’ve got to support the people who are actually doing the work. That’s Ruben, and we know it would mean a lot to him if you signed on.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/signup/260904-personal-endorse-em/?source=em260905-1-160&refcode2=4200.734936.VZ-vgN&akid=4200%2E734936%2EVZ-vgN)

Thank you,
Team Gallego

name: Roy Cooper
subject: Too close for comfort
body:
What just happened in North Carolina.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1278&source=&t=1&akid=3201%2E124072%2E7jM4NK) | | | |
---
There’s been a huge development in the race, Peter. Let me explain.
**As I write this, the GOP is going all in to defeat me.** President Trump has endorsed my MAGA opponent and personally attacked me on social media, Stephen Miller recently went on Fox News to rant and rave about me and super PACs are putting hundreds of millions behind baseless ads lying about who I am and what I’m fighting for.
They’re coming after me so hard because they know that if they can just defeat us, it won’t matter what happens in other swing states. If the GOP wins NC, that’s the ballgame – they’ll likely keep U.S. Senate control until 2029.
Unfortunately, these attacks are working.**A recent poll shows that this race is once again statistically tied.**
This comes just a few weeks after the Senate GOP's top super PAC launched new TV ads all across the state, which they had originally planned to start airing _this month._
They’re spending tens of millions so far in North Carolina to defeat me, and the polls show that their investments are paying off.
**I need your help, Peter. We’re getting outspent, and without your immediate grassroots support, we could put our shot at flipping this seat at risk.[_So if you care about winning in North Carolina and retaking the Senate, making a well-timed donation of $5 to my campaign today is the best thing you can do to help me fight back, protect our narrowing lead and win. Please, will you chip in?_](https://act.roycooper.com/go/8283?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1278&amount=5&t=8&akid=3201%2E124072%2E7jM4NK)**

subject: They told me I could count on you
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Rogers for Senate
body:
| | | | | A Personal Message From Mike
---
Peter,
---
I am reaching out to you directly because, quite frankly, I don't know where else to turn. I've spent the last few hours pacing the room, trying to process what is happening. The latest developments are incredibly daunting, and my heart is heavy with an overwhelming sense of urgency.

Friend,

No parent should ever have to wonder if they will make it home to see their children at the end of the workday.
No child should have to watch masked federal agents in tactical gear pull neighbors out of cars as their school bus rolls down the street.
And no family in Connecticut – or anywhere in America – should have to live in fear of unmarked vehicles cruising through their neighborhoods.
This isn’t something happening in a distant corner of the country. It’s happening right here in our home state.
Just last week in Danbury, ICE deployed a massive, aggressive enforcement sweep that resulted in dozens of people being detained. They swarmed supermarkets, parks, and even school zones. We’ve seen horrific reports of unconstitutional racial profiling, agents using Tasers on men lying face-down on the asphalt, and federal officers denying families and legal counsel access to their loved ones in local hospitals.
Let’s be completely clear: ICE is terrorizing our communities with illegal, abusive, and abhorrent tactics.
Snatching people off our streets as they walk their kids to school or wait for a ride to work isn’t justice – it is a plain-and-simple abuse of federal power. It strips away human dignity, tears apart families, and instills raw fear into the places we call home.
**As Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, I have launched a formal inquiry into ICE’s unlawful tactics and training. But to stop these atrocities and hold these agents and the Trump administration accountable, I need the full power of our movement standing with me.**
